definition_en: a system that uses radio waves to detect objects and measure their position; the equipment used for this; an ability to notice things quickly
core_image: 绿色屏幕上缓慢移动的一个亮点，边缘带着淡淡的余辉
scene: 值班室里，绿色屏幕上出现一个缓慢移动的亮点，值班员记下方位和距离。 The tiny blip on the radar was a fishing boat lost in the fog.
sceneCN: 这里 radar 是「雷达」（第 1 个义项：用无线电波探测物体位置的系统）；句意为雷达上那个小小的光点是一艘在雾中迷失的渔船。画面里可留意：绿色屏幕、移动的亮点、记录方位的手。

collocations.zh: 在雷达上；在关注范围内

derivatives.zh: radar 与 scope 复合，指雷达显示器
radar 与 man 复合，指操作雷达的人员
radar 与 dome 缩合，指保护雷达天线的罩壳

senses.title: A radio detection system
senses.definition: a system that sends out radio waves and reads the echoes to find objects and their positions
senses.definitionCN: 发出无线电波并读取回声，以发现物体及其位置的系统
senses.example: The plane appeared on radar at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，那架飞机出现在雷达上。
senses.why: The word is an acronym built from radio detection and ranging, so the name describes exactly what the system does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是由「无线电探测与测距」的首字母拼成的缩略词，名字正好描述了该系统所做的事。

senses.title: The equipment itself
senses.definition: the set of apparatus that produces and receives the radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 产生并接收无线电波的一整套设备
senses.example: The ship's radar failed in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘船的雷达在雾中失灵了。
senses.why: Once the system had a name, the physical set that contains it took the same name, as happens with many devices.
senses.whyCN: 这套系统有了名字之后，装着它的实体设备也叫同一个名字，许多器械都是如此。

senses.title: A knack for noticing things
senses.definition: an informal ability to sense or notice things that others miss
senses.definitionCN: 一种察觉他人忽略之事的非正式能力
senses.example: She has a radar for insincerity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对虚情假意有一种敏锐的直觉。
senses.why: A device that detects what the eye cannot see became a metaphor for a person who notices what others miss.
senses.whyCN: 一种能察觉肉眼看不见之物的人造装置，成了「能注意到他人忽略之事的人」的比喻。

intro.en: Radar is a twentieth-century acronym, not an inherited word; it was coined from the initials of radio detection and ranging.
intro.cn: radar 是二十世纪的缩略词，不是继承下来的词；它由「无线电探测与测距」的首字母拼成。

items.en: Radio waves could be bounced off objects, and the returning echo carried information about distance and direction.
items.cn: 无线电波可以从物体上反弹，返回的回声携带着距离与方向的信息。

items.en: Ranging meant measuring distance, and the time an echo takes gives the distance of the object that reflected it.
items.cn: ranging 意为测距，回声所用的时间可以给出反射它的物体的距离。

items.en: The initials of the phrase were joined into one pronounceable word during the nineteen forties.
items.cn: 这个短语的首字母在二十世纪四十年代被拼成一个可读的词。

items.en: The device was developed for detecting aircraft and ships, and the short name made it easy to say in a hurry.
items.cn: 这种装置为探测飞机与船只而发展起来，简短的名字让人在匆忙中也容易说出口。

items.en: Modern English uses radar for the device, for the technique and, figuratively, for a person's alertness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radar 指设备、技术，也比喻一个人的警觉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on the acronym; the near-meaning group gathers words for detection and sensing.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个缩略词构成的复合词；近义组收表示探测与感知的词。

entries.definition: The screen that displays radar returns.
A person who operates radar equipment.
A cover that protects a radar antenna.
The technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves.
entries.definitionCN: 用电磁波传送信号的技术，radar 的前半部分即由此而来。

entries.definition: The act of discovering something that is present.
Following the movement of something over time.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间追踪某物的运动。

entries.definition: A device that responds to something in its surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 对周围事物作出反应的装置。

entries.definition: A system that detects objects under water by sound.
entries.definitionCN: 用水下声波探测物体的系统。

normalIntro.en: The name is an acronym, so its five letters carry the whole method: send radio waves, hear the echo, measure the time.
normalIntro.cn: 名字本身就是缩略词，五个字母承载了整套方法：发出无线电波、听回声、算时间。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging shortened to its initials, which is why the word has no ordinary root.
normal.cn: radar 是 radio detection and ranging 的首字母缩写，所以它没有平常意义上的词根。

normal.en: On the radar means being noticed or watched, taken from the glowing blip on a screen.
normal.cn: on the radar 指被注意或被关注，来自屏幕上发亮的光点。

normal.en: Under the radar means going unnoticed, as a plane that does not show up on the screen.
normal.cn: under the radar 指不被注意，像一架不在屏幕上显示的飞机。

normal.en: Sonar is the underwater cousin: sound navigation and ranging, built the same acronym way.
normal.cn: sonar 是它水下的亲戚：声呐导航与测距，同样用缩略法造出。

normal.en: A radar for insincerity is a metaphor: the person detects what others fail to see.
normal.cn: a radar for insincerity 是比喻：这个人能察觉别人看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radar taught the modern world to trust what cannot be seen, as long as a machine reports it.
abstract.cn: 雷达教会现代世界去相信看不见的东西，只要有一台机器报告它。

abstract.en: The same word now names a device and a human gift, because both mean noticing what is out of sight.
abstract.cn: 同一个词现在既指装置也指人的天赋，因为两者都意味着察觉视线之外的东西。

abstract.en: Every detection system defines what counts as a signal, and that definition is a human choice inside a machine.
abstract.cn: 每一套探测系统都要界定什么算作信号，而这个界定是机器内部的人为选择。

examples.en: The storm showed up on radar two hours before it arrived.
examples.cn: 暴风雨到达前两小时就在雷达上出现了。

examples.en: The coast guard uses radar to find boats in heavy fog.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用雷达在浓雾中寻找船只。

examples.en: He has a radar for people who are only pretending to listen.
examples.cn: 他对那些假装在听的人有一种敏锐的直觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「雷打」——雷打一样的电波扫出去，碰到东西就弹回来，记住 radar 是雷达。

root: 二十世纪缩略词，由 radio detection and ranging（无线电探测与测距）的首字母拼成；没有拉丁语词源。同族有 radarscope、radarman、radome。

sensesIntro.en: The core is detection by echo; the senses divide into the system, the equipment and the figurative alertness of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠回声探测」；义项分为系统本身、设备本身，以及比喻意义上人的警觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single bright blip drifting across a green screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮的光点在绿色屏幕上缓缓移动。

branches.en: a wave leaving an antenna and returning
branches.cn: 从天线发出又返回的一道波

branches.en: a cabinet of dials below a screen
branches.cn: 屏幕下方一排旋钮的机柜

branches.en: a host noticing a guest's false smile
branches.cn: 主人察觉到客人虚假的笑容

branches.en: the method and the box that carries it out
branches.cn: 方法与实现它的那只箱子

branches.en: the same noticing, once by a machine and once by a mind
branches.cn: 同一种察觉，一次由机器，一次由头脑

intro.en: The word is an acronym, so its parts are the initials of English technical terms rather than roots or affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，它的组成部分是英语技术术语的首字母，而不是词根或词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word, which was coined in the twentieth century.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是二十世纪新造的，没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视
definition_en: an instrument that makes very small objects look large enough to examine; also any high-power instrument of this kind and a figurative state of close scrutiny
core_image: 一枚镜片把叶片上的小格子放大到眼前
scene: 实验台上摆着切片和光源，学生们轮流俯身看那片薄薄的叶片。 Through the microscope, the leaf showed rows of tiny green cells.
sceneCN: 这里是「显微镜」（第 1 个义项：放大微小物体的仪器）；句意为透过显微镜，叶片显出成排的绿色小细胞。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、载玻片、叶片。

pos.zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视

collocations.zh: 在显微镜下；受到严密审视

derivatives.zh: 由 microscope 词干加 -ic 构成，义为「显微镜的；小到看不见的」
由 microscope 词干加 -y 构成，义为「显微镜术；显微检查」
由 microscope 加 -ist 构成，义为「显微镜使用者；显微镜专家」

senses.title: An instrument that magnifies small things
senses.definition: a scientific instrument with lenses that makes very small objects look large enough to examine
senses.definitionCN: 装有透镜、能把极小的物体放大到足以观察的科学仪器
senses.example: Under the microscope, the onion skin showed neat rows of cells.
senses.exampleCN: 在显微镜下，洋葱表皮显出一排排整齐的细胞。
senses.why: Greek skopein meant to look, so with mikros small the compound literally names a way of looking at what the eye cannot see, and the instrument inherited that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 skopein 意为「看」，与表示「小」的 mikros 组合，字面上就是「观看小东西的方式」，仪器便继承了这个名字。

senses.title: A high-power instrument using electrons or other radiation
senses.definition: any of the more powerful instruments that form an image with electron beams or other radiation instead of ordinary light
senses.definitionCN: 用电子束或其他辐射代替普通光成像的更高倍率的各类显微设备
senses.example: An electron microscope revealed the virus in fine detail.
senses.exampleCN: 电子显微镜把病毒的细节清晰地显现出来。
senses.why: When glass lenses reached their limit, the same word was stretched to instruments that no longer use light, because the purpose rather than the optics is what the name marks.
senses.whyCN: 当玻璃透镜放大到极限，这个词又被延伸到不再用光的仪器上，因为命名看重的是用途，而不是光学原理。

senses.title: Close, searching examination
senses.definition: a situation of being examined very closely, as in the fixed phrase under the microscope
senses.definitionCN: 处于被极为仔细检查的境地，常见于 under the microscope 这一说法
senses.example: After the leak, the whole department was under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 泄密事件之后，整个部门都处在严密审视之下。
senses.why: A microscope exposes what is invisible to the naked eye, so putting a person or an institution under one means even the smallest faults are being looked at.
senses.whyCN: 显微镜把肉眼看不见的东西摊开，因此把人或机构放在显微镜下，就等于连最细小的毛病都要被看清。

intro.en: Microscope joins two Greek words, small and to look, was given a modern Latin form, and entered English in the seventeenth century as lens-making improved.
intro.cn: microscope 把两个希腊词「小」与「看」接在一起，先有近代拉丁语形式，再在十七世纪透镜工艺进步时进入英语。

items.en: Mikros meant small, and it supplied the first element for instruments that work at a scale the eye cannot reach.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的，为那些在人眼够不着的尺度上工作的仪器提供了第一个词素。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at or examine, and its combining form -scope later named many viewing instruments.
items.cn: skopein 意为看、察看，它的构词形式 -scope 后来命名了许多观察仪器。

items.en: Early scientists gave the new instrument a Latin name from the two Greek elements before any English word existed for it.
items.cn: 早期的科学家用这两个希腊词素给新仪器起了拉丁名，当时英语里还没有对应的词。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century as lens grinding made single-lens instruments practical for naturalists.
items.cn: 十七世纪，随着透镜研磨技术让单透镜仪器对博物学者变得实用，英语采纳了这个词。

items.en: The compound now covers electron and other advanced instruments, and its prepositional phrase has become a metaphor for close scrutiny.
items.cn: 这个复合词现在涵盖了电子显微镜等进阶设备，它的介词短语也成了「严密审视」的比喻说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the small plus look pattern and its derived family; the near-meaning group collects the glass and the specimens that go with the instrument.
note.cn: 形近组顺着「小」加「看」的构词模式与派生词族；近义组收与这种仪器配套的镜片和标本。

entries.definition: Too small to be seen without an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 小到不用仪器就看不见的。

entries.definition: The technique of examining things with a microscope.
entries.definitionCN: 用显微镜检查事物的技术。

entries.definition: An instrument for viewing distant objects.
An instrument for looking over or around an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 越过或绕过障碍观察的仪器。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass that bends light to form an image.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的玻璃片，使光折射成像。

entries.definition: A hand-held lens used to make small things look larger.
entries.definitionCN: 手持透镜，把小的东西放大来看。

entries.definition: A thin glass plate on which a specimen is placed for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 放置标本供观察的薄玻璃片。

entries.definition: A small sample of something kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 留作研究用的少量样品。

normalIntro.en: Small plus looking: the compound names an instrument that does not enlarge the object but brings it close enough for the eye.
normalIntro.cn: 「小」加「看」：这个复合词命名的仪器并不把物体变大，而是把它拉到眼睛够得近的地方。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -scope comes from the Greek verb for looking, so the word spells out looking at small things.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-scope 出自希腊语中表示「看」的动词，这个词把「看小东西」直接拼了出来。

normal.en: Telescope uses the same -scope element for far objects, and periscope uses it for looking around.
normal.cn: telescope 用同一个 -scope 词素看远处，periscope 用它绕过障碍看。

normal.en: Microscopic adds -ic and describes what is too small for the unaided eye.
normal.cn: microscopic 加了 -ic，形容小到肉眼无法看清的东西。

normal.en: Microscopy names the technique, and a microscopist is the person who performs it.
normal.cn: microscopy 指这门技术，microscopist 指操作它的人。

normal.en: Under the microscope is a fixed phrase that moved from the lab bench into everyday talk about scrutiny.
normal.cn: under the microscope 是固定说法，已经从实验台走进日常语言，指严密审查。

abstract.en: The glass does not enlarge the cell; it only shortens the distance between the cell and your attention.
abstract.cn: 镜片并不把细胞变大，只是缩短了细胞与你注意力之间的距离。

abstract.en: Looking closely rewrites what you see: a plain leaf becomes rows of green rooms.
abstract.cn: 凑近看会改写你所见的：一片普通的叶子变成一排排绿色的小房间。

abstract.en: A lens became a word for scrutiny, because attention magnifies faults just as glass magnifies cells.
abstract.cn: 一片镜片变成了「审视」的代名词，因为注意力放大过失，就像镜片放大细胞一样。

examples.en: The students took turns looking through the microscope.
examples.cn: 学生们轮流透过显微镜观察。

examples.en: An electron microscope can show the shape of a virus.
examples.cn: 电子显微镜能显示病毒的形状。

examples.en: After the audit, the whole office was under the microscope.
examples.cn: 审计之后，整个办公室都处在严密审视之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克看」——麦克凑近镜片看小虫，看小东西的镜子就是显微镜。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 skopein（看）拼接，经近代科学拉丁语 microscopium 进入英语，指观察微小物体的仪器；没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is looking at what is too small; the senses divide into the lens instrument, the powered instruments that replaced light, and the scrutiny those instruments symbolize.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「观看过小的东西」；义项分到透镜仪器、取代光的强力设备，以及这类仪器所象征的严密审视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lens bringing the cells of a leaf close enough for the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚镜片把叶片上的细胞拉到眼前。

branches.en: onion cells lined up under a lens
branches.cn: 透镜下排成行的洋葱细胞

branches.en: an electron beam tracing a virus
branches.cn: 电子束扫出病毒的轮廓

branches.en: a department watched after a leak
branches.cn: 泄密之后被盯住的部门

branches.en: detail revealed first by light and then by electrons
branches.cn: 细节先由光显现，再由电子显现

branches.en: the same act of looking closely, at cells and at people
branches.cn: 同一个凑近细看的动作，一次对细胞，一次对人

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek look-element form the word, and English suffixes later build the technique and the person around it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「看」的希腊词素构成这个词，英语后缀后来又在它周围造出技术与人的名称。

latinIntro.en: The word was formed from Greek elements and given a modern Latin shape by early scientists, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词由希腊词素构成，早期科学家只给了它一个近代拉丁语外形，古典拉丁语中没有同族词记录。

definition_en: the state of not being able to do something, usually because of a lack of power, skill, or a chance
core_image: 一双手被绑在身后，面前是一扇明明没锁却推不开的门
scene: 志愿队赶到山里的第二天，担架不够，医生的手再稳也抬不动那么多人。 His inability to speak the local language made the first week very slow.
sceneCN: 这里 inability 是「无法、没有能力」（第 1 个义项：因为缺条件而做不成），句意是他不会说当地话，头一周进展极慢。画面里有山里的医疗点、一双稳当的手和担架。

pos.zh: 名词：无能力、无法（做某事），常与 to do 或 to 名词连用

collocations.zh: 对自己无能为力的沮丧

derivatives.zh: 能力（加否定前缀 in- 构成反义）
不能的、不会的
复数：若干方面的不足

senses.title: Lacking the power to do something
senses.definition: the fact of not being able to do something because the power or skill is absent
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少力量或技能而做不到某件事
senses.example: The disease causes a gradual inability to walk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病会导致逐步无法行走。
senses.why: The noun names a state rather than an act, so it usually appears with a following to-clause or noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指一种状态而非动作，所以通常跟一个 to 加动词或名词的说明。

senses.title: Not being allowed or unable by circumstance
senses.definition: the position of being unable to act because of money, rules, or other outside limits
senses.definitionCN: 因钱、规定或其他外部限制而无法行动
senses.example: Their inability to pay the rent was the real cause of the move.
senses.exampleCN: 他们无力付房租才是搬家的真正原因。
senses.why: Here the lack is not in the person but in the situation, and the noun describes that pressure.
senses.whyCN: 此时缺的不是人的本事，而是条件，名词描述的是那种压强。

senses.title: A particular weakness
senses.definition: one specific thing a person or a system cannot do well
senses.definitionCN: 人或系统在某个具体方面做不好
senses.example: The report lists the company's inabilities without much softening.
senses.exampleCN: 报告直白列出了这家公司的短处。
senses.why: Made countable, the noun points to individual gaps rather than a general state.
senses.whyCN: 变成可数后，名词指向一项项具体的缺口，而不是总体状态。

intro.en: Inability is the negative of ability, and both rest on a Latin word for being skilful or fit.
intro.cn: inability 是 ability 的否定形式，两者都建在拉丁语中表示「能干、合适」的词上。

items.en: Habere meant to hold, and habilis described something easy to hold or handle, hence handy and fit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 habere 意为「持握」，形容词 habilis 形容好用、好拿，引申为「合适、能干」。

items.en: The noun habilitas named the quality of being fit for a task, especially in law about rights.
items.cn: 名词 habilitas 指适合做某事的资格，尤用于法律中关于权利的说法。

items.en: French reshaped it as habilite, then ablete, meaning skill or competence.
items.cn: 法语把它改作 habilite，又作 ablete，意为技能与胜任之力。

items.en: English took ability in the fourteenth century, and inability followed quickly as its plain opposite.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪收下 ability，inability 作为其朴素的反面很快跟上。

items.en: Medicine and law made inability a formal word for a lasting loss of power or of a legal right.
items.cn: 医学与法律把 inability 变成正式用词，指能力或法律资格的持续缺失。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the -ility family; the near-meaning group gathers words for lacking power.
note.cn: 形近组收 -ility 一族词；近义组收表示「缺少力量」的词。

entries.definition: The positive twin, meaning skill or the power to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式「能力、才能」，是 inability 的正对面。

entries.definition: A tendency to change or fall over, not a lack of skill.
entries.definitionCN: 「不稳定」，指容易变化或失衡，并非缺少技能。

entries.definition: The state of not noticing or not caring.
entries.definitionCN: 「不敏感、不体谅」，同为 in- 加 -ility 的构造。

entries.definition: The feeling of having no control over events.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「无力感」，强调对局面毫无掌控。

entries.definition: A formal word for being unable, often because of health or law.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「无行为能力」，正式用语，多因健康或法律原因。

entries.definition: A lack of success in doing something actually attempted.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「失败」，指尝试了却没成功，与「做不到」有别。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the negative prefix and the sentence frames that inability almost always appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用否定前缀，以及 inability 几乎总出现在其中的句式。

normal.en: in plus ability makes it clear: take the skill away and you get inability.
normal.cn: in 加 ability 一目了然：把本事拿走，剩下的就是 inability。

normal.en: Inability almost always takes to: inability to sleep, to pay, to read.
normal.cn: inability 后面几乎总接 to：inability to sleep、to pay、to read。

normal.en: It is a state, not a failed attempt, so it is not the same as failure.
normal.cn: 它是一种状态，而不是一次失败的尝试，所以不等于 failure。

normal.en: Hospitals and contracts prefer inability because it sounds neutral and lasting.
normal.cn: 医院与合同偏爱 inability，因为它听起来中性且指较持久的情形。

normal.en: When you want the adjective instead of the noun, use unable to do.
normal.cn: 如果要形容词而不是名词，就用 unable to do。

abstract.en: Naming an inability is usually a first step in asking for help, which is why the word sounds quietly honest.
abstract.cn: 说出「做不到」往往就是求援的第一步，所以这个词听来有种安静的诚实。

abstract.en: The root for ability meant easy to hold, so ability is always about fitting a task, not about being better in the abstract.
abstract.cn: ability 的词根意为「好拿」，所以能力始终是说「适合某项任务」，而非抽象地更强。

abstract.en: Most social inabilities are misnamed; what is called inability is often a lack of permission.
abstract.cn: 许多所谓「做不到」其实是被叫错了名字，真正缺的常是许可，而非能力。

examples.en: His inability to remember names embarrasses him at parties.
examples.cn: 他记不住名字，在聚会上常为此尴尬。

examples.en: The village's inability to reach a doctor was solved by a mobile clinic.
examples.cn: 村里看病难的问题靠一辆流动诊所解决了。

examples.en: She spoke openly about her inabilities as a young teacher.
examples.cn: 她坦率谈起自己当年轻老师时的种种短板。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 不 + ability 能力——能力被拿走的状态，就是「做不到」

root: 由否定前缀 in- 加 ability 构成；ability 出自拉丁语 habilitas「适合做某事的资质」，源自 habilis「好持握、灵巧」，经古法语进入中世纪英语，inability 随之出现，后成为医学与法律中的正式用词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: lacking power or skill, being blocked by outside conditions, and one particular weakness.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：缺本事，被外部条件卡住，以及某一方面的具体短处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands tied behind the back in front of an unlocked door that will not open.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手被绑在身后，面前是一扇没锁却推不开的门。

branches.en: THE SKILL: the missing thing may be training or strength.
branches.cn: 本事线：缺的可能是训练，也可能是力气。

branches.en: THE MEANS: money and rules can produce the same state.
branches.cn: 条件线：钱和规定也能造出同样的状态。

branches.en: THE LIST: plural inabilities itemise separate gaps.
branches.cn: 清单线：复数形式把短板一项项列出来。

branches.en: THE FRAME: inability to do something is the fixed pattern.
branches.cn: 句式线：inability to do something 是固定框架。

branches.en: THE PAIR: ability and inability stand on the same Latin root.
branches.cn: 对照线：ability 与 inability 站在同一拉丁词根上。

definition_zh: 地下的；秘密的；地下组织；（英）地铁
definition_en: below the surface of the ground, or hidden from public view
core_image: 在土层之下，一条亮着灯的线路悄悄延伸
scene: 冬天地面结着薄冰，人们缩着脖子下到楼梯深处，那里暖风阵阵、车灯闪动。 They took the underground across the city.
sceneCN: 这里 underground 是「地铁（英式）」（第 2 个义项：地下的交通系统）；句意为他们乘地铁穿城而过。土层下亮灯延伸的线路，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀的原词，义为「地面；场地」

senses.title: Below the surface of the earth
senses.definition: placed or happening under the surface of the ground
senses.definitionCN: 位于或发生于地表之下
senses.example: The city built a huge underground car park.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市建了一个巨大的地下停车场。
senses.why: Ground is the surface we stand on, and under puts the whole system beneath it.
senses.whyCN: ground 是我们脚下的地表，under 把整套东西放到它下面。

senses.title: A city railway below the streets
senses.definition: the railway system that runs in tunnels under a city
senses.definitionCN: 在城市街道下方的隧道中运行的铁路系统
senses.example: The underground is quicker than the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 地铁比公交车快。
senses.why: Londoners shortened the full name to the underground, and the noun took over.
senses.whyCN: 伦敦人把这套系统的全名缩作 the underground，名词就此定型。

senses.title: Hidden and against the authorities
senses.definition: of a movement or publication, operating in secret against a government
senses.definitionCN: 指运动或出版物在暗处与政府对抗
senses.example: The novel was passed around in underground copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以地下本的形式流传。
senses.why: To operate underground is literally to be out of sight, and secrecy borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 在地下活动字面上就是见不到光，秘密也就借用了这张图。

senses.title: To go into hiding
senses.definition: of a person or group, to disappear from public life
senses.definitionCN: 指人或团体从公众生活中消失
senses.example: The writer went underground for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家隐没了十年。
senses.why: When someone sinks below the surface, they can no longer be found by ordinary means.
senses.whyCN: 一个人沉到地表之下，常规手段就找不到他了。

senses.title: Secret and unofficial
senses.definition: existing in secret without official approval
senses.definitionCN: 未经官方许可而在暗中存在的
senses.example: An underground economy grew along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 边境上长出了一片地下经济。
senses.why: Money that never enters the books lives, in effect, below the visible streets.
senses.whyCN: 从不进账的钱，实际上就生活在看得见的街道下面。

examples.en: She asked the salesman for a receipt.
examples.cn: 她向售货员要了收据。

examples.en: The insurance salesman explained the policy.
examples.cn: 保险推销员解释了保单。

dict_mnemonic.text: sales（销售）加 man（人）：做销售的男人，就是 salesman（推销员）。

root: 由 sales（销售）与 man（人）复合而成，核心义「以销售商品为职的男子」。

sensesIntro.en: Salesman means a man who sells in a shop, a travelling seller, or a company representative.
sensesIntro.cn: salesman 意为商店男售货员、巡回推销员，或公司销售代表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a sample case at a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：提着样品箱站在门口的人。

branches.en: The base sense is a man who sells in a shop.
branches.cn: 基础义是在商店卖货的男子。

branches.en: Shop selling becomes selling on the road.
branches.cn: 店内销售变成上门推销。

branches.en: The seller becomes a company representative.
branches.cn: 销售者变成公司代表。

branches.en: Shop assistants and travelling sellers both sell.
branches.cn: 店员与巡回推销员都在销售。

branches.en: Travelling sellers often represent a company.
branches.cn: 巡回推销员常常代表公司。

intro.en: Salesman is a compound of sales and man, with a neutral form salesperson.
intro.cn: salesman 是 sales 与 man 的复合词，中性形式是 salesperson。

latinIntro.en: Salesman has no Latin root; both parts are English.
latinIntro.cn: salesman 没有拉丁词根，两个部分都来自英语。

items.exampleCN: 推销员们每天早上开会。
好的推销术能建立信任。

items.meaning: the activity or total of selling

items.example: The vendor sold fruit at the market.

definition_zh: 向上；往上；以上；朝上游；向更高处、更高水平
definition_en: towards a higher place, level or amount
core_image: 一只手指着楼梯上方的台阶，视线跟着一级一级抬上去
scene: 电梯显示屏上的数字一格一格往上跳，停在顶层时门才打开。 She turned her eyes upwards to the top of the tower.
sceneCN: 这里 upwards 是「向上、朝上」（第 1 个义项：朝更高的地方）；句意为她抬眼望向塔顶。手指与视线一同抬高的方向，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 副词：向上、往上；以上；向更高水平

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「向上的、上升的」，ups 去掉尾缀就是它
副词，义为「向上、起来」，是 upwards 的词干
反义词，意为「向下」
加 -ly 构成，义为「向上地」，常见于 upwardly mobile

senses.title: Towards a higher place
senses.definition: towards a higher position in space
senses.definitionCN: 朝空间中更高的位置
senses.example: She turned her eyes upwards to the top of the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 她抬眼望向塔顶。
senses.why: The base word up already names the direction; the suffix only points the movement onwards.
senses.whyCN: 词干 up 本身已经指明方向，后缀只是让这个方向继续延伸。

senses.title: A larger amount
senses.titleCN: 以上：数量超过某个整数
senses.definition: more than a stated number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 超过所说的数字或数量
senses.example: Upwards of three hundred people attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 参加会议的有三百人以上。
senses.why: A quantity climbing up the number line behaves like a body climbing stairs.
senses.whyCN: 数量沿数轴往上爬，就像身体沿楼梯往上走。

senses.title: Towards a higher level
senses.titleCN: 向更高水平：地位或数值上升
senses.definition: towards a higher standard, rank or price
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的标准、等级或价格
senses.example: Prices have moved steadily upwards this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年物价稳步上涨。
senses.why: The spatial direction is borrowed for abstract scales; higher on a chart is more.
senses.whyCN: 空间方向被借到抽象尺度上：图表里越高就是越多。

senses.title: Up the river
senses.titleCN: 朝上游：往河的内陆方向
senses.definition: along a river towards its source, away from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 沿河朝源头方向、远离大海
senses.example: The boat moved slowly upwards along the narrow river.
senses.exampleCN: 小船沿着狭窄的河道慢慢向上游行驶。
senses.why: Rivers flow down to the sea, so walking inland means walking up the water.
senses.whyCN: 河水向下流向大海，所以往内陆走就是往水的上方走。

intro.en: Upwards joins the old adverb up to the direction suffix -weard, which survives in towards and forwards.
intro.cn: upwards 由古老的副词 up 加上方向后缀 -weard 构成，同款后缀还留在 towards 与 forwards 里。

items.en: Old English had uppweard, built from upp, up, plus the direction suffix -weard, turned towards.
items.cn: 古英语已有 uppweard，由 upp「向上」加方向后缀 -weard「朝向」构成。

items.en: The Norse form upp reinforced the northern dialects, giving the hard p still heard today.
items.cn: 古诺斯的 upp 强化了北方方言，留下今天仍能听到的清晰辅音。

items.en: Middle English wrote upward, still used in American spelling and in the adverb of direction.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 upward，这一形式仍用于美式拼写和方向副词。

items.en: The southern -s form won as the British adverb, while the adjective kept the short form upward.
items.cn: 带 s 的南方形式成为英式副词的标准形式，而形容词保留了短的 upward。

items.en: Today upwards of a number means more than it, a phrase fixed in nineteenth century commercial writing.
items.cn: 如今 upwards of 加数字表示「超过」，这个说法在十九世纪商业文书中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the -wards family; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of rising.
note.cn: 形近组收同一组 -wards 方向词；近义组收表示上升的副词。

entries.definition: Towards the back; the same -wards ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向后」，同样带 -wards 尾缀。

entries.definition: Towards the front; another direction of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向前」，同一词族的另一个方向。

entries.definition: In the direction of; the suffix here marks a target.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝向」，这里的尾缀标记目标。

entries.definition: At a later time; the same suffix used for time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后」，同款尾缀用在了时间上。

entries.definition: The same direction, usual as an adjective or in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或美式副词，义为「向上的」，方向相同。

entries.definition: High up in the air; a more literary way to say upwards.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在高处」，更文学化的说法。

entries.definition: Towards the sky; upward with a picture attached.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「朝天空」，是带画面的向上。

entries.definition: At a higher position than something else, often static.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……上方」，多指静态位置。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the direction suffix and on the phrase upwards of that appears in real news copy.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借方向后缀与真实新闻里常见的 upwards of 搭配。

normal.en: upwards is up plus a suffix that means turned towards.
normal.cn: upwards 就是 up 加上一个意为「朝向」的后缀。

normal.en: Upwards of fifty means more than fifty, not exactly fifty.
normal.cn: upwards of fifty 指超过五十，而不是正好五十。

normal.en: Stairs, prices and ages can all go upwards.
normal.cn: 楼梯、价格和年龄都可以往上走。

normal.en: The British write upwards, Americans often write upward.
normal.cn: 英式写 upwards，美式常写 upward。

normal.en: Looking upwards is a body movement before it is a metaphor.
normal.cn: 抬头向上首先是身体动作，然后才是比喻。

abstract.en: Every upward movement in the word is a number line: a place, a sum, a rank, each one higher.
abstract.cn: 这个词里每一种向上都是同一条数轴：位置、数量、等级，一个比一个高。

abstract.en: The suffix quietly says which way; the stem says how far, and the two are enough for a whole direction.
abstract.cn: 后缀悄悄说明朝哪边，词干说明朝哪里去，两者合起来就够表示一个完整方向。

abstract.en: When a word can climb stairs and prices at once, it is really describing one habit of the mind: rising.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能爬楼梯又能涨价格，它其实在描述心智的一个习惯：上升。

examples.en: The path climbs upwards through a narrow valley.
examples.cn: 小路穿过狭窄的山谷一路向上。

examples.en: Upwards of two thousand visitors came on the first day.
examples.cn: 第一天来的游客有两千以上。

examples.en: He glanced upwards at the darkening sky.
examples.cn: 他抬头看了看渐渐暗下来的天空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆往兹」——阿婆往兹（兹）边上一抬头，就是往上

root: 由古英语 upp「向上」加方向后缀 -weard 构成，古英语作 uppweard，中古英语作 upward，南部的 -s 形式固定为英式副词 upwards；同族词有 up、upward、forwards、towards。

sensesIntro.en: Upwards moves between space, number, scale and river, always in the same direction.
sensesIntro.cn: upwards 在空间、数量、尺度与河道之间移动，方向始终一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip climbs from one step to the next, never pointing down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指从一级台阶抬到下一级，从不下指。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: eyes and feet move to a higher place.
branches.cn: 空间线：眼睛和双脚移向更高的地方。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: amounts and levels climb above their old values.
branches.cn: 数量线：数量与水平爬过原来的数值。

branches.en: RIVER LINE: the boat heads inland, away from the sea.
branches.cn: 河道线：小船朝内陆驶去，远离大海。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the head tilts back to see the top.
branches.cn: 身体线：头向后仰去看顶部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: upwards of is a floor, not a ceiling.
branches.cn: 对照线：upwards of 给的是下限，不是上限。

intro.en: Upwards is a stem plus a direction suffix, then a plural-looking s; each part is real and old.
intro.cn: upwards 由词干、方向后缀和看似复数的 s 组成，每一部分都有真实的老来源。

latinIntro.en: No Latin is involved here; the word is Germanic through and through.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词与拉丁语无关，从头到尾都是日耳曼来源。

items.example: It is the core of upwards.

items.meaning: of the manner, later just an adverb
items.example: It marks the southern adverb form.
items.exampleCN: 它标记南方的副词形式。

items.example: It shows the suffix at work.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了这个后缀的作用。

items.example: It is the reverse of upwards.
items.exampleCN: 它是 upwards 的反向词。

items.example: It uses down instead of up.
items.exampleCN: 它把 up 换成了 down。

definition_zh: 保守的；守旧的；谨慎的；保守派；偏低的
definition_en: preferring old ways and slow change, cautious, or a deliberately low estimate
core_image: 老人试了新沙发，还是坐回那张旧木椅
scene: 搬家后老人试了试新沙发，又坐回旧木椅。 He gave a conservative estimate of the cost.
sceneCN: 这里 conservative 指「偏低的；谨慎的」（第 3 个义项：估计故意低于真实数字）；句意是他对费用给出了一个偏低的估计。

derivatives.zh: 保护；节约
保护；保存；节约
保守主义
保守地；谨慎地

senses.title: Preferring the old
senses.definition: preferring traditional ways and slow change
senses.definitionCN: 偏好传统方式与缓慢的改变
senses.example: His family is conservative about clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他家人对穿着比较保守。
senses.why: What has lasted feels safer than what is only new.
senses.whyCN: 已经延续下来的东西，比只是新鲜的东西更让人安心。

senses.title: Cautious
senses.definition: careful and not willing to take risks
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎而不愿承担风险
senses.example: The bank took a conservative view of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 银行对市场持谨慎看法。
senses.why: A low guess is a cushion against being wrong.
senses.whyCN: 把话说低一点，是给判断失误留的垫子。

senses.title: A low estimate
senses.definition: deliberately below the real figure
senses.definitionCN: 故意低于真实数字的
senses.example: He gave a conservative estimate of the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他对费用给出了一个偏低的估计。
senses.why: Promise little, and the final number can only surprise upward.
senses.whyCN: 把话说小，最后的数字只可能向上给人惊喜。

intro.en: Conservative comes from Latin conservare, to keep safe, from com-, together, and servare, to keep.
intro.cn: conservative 来自拉丁语 conservare，意为保全，由 com-（一起）与 servare（保存）构成。

items.en: Servare meant to keep and guard.
items.cn: servare 意为保存与看守。

items.en: Conservare meant to keep something whole.
items.cn: conservare 意为使某物保持完整。

items.en: Conservativus described a power that preserves.
items.cn: conservativus 描述一种具保存作用的力量。

items.en: English conservative first meant having the power to preserve.
items.cn: 英语 conservative 最初指具有保存作用的。

items.en: It became a political label for those slow to change.
items.cn: 它成为指称不愿急变者的政治标签。

items.en: It also means a careful, low estimate.
items.cn: 它也表示谨慎而偏低的估计。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of conservative, and the meaning group names related habits of caution or tradition.
note.cn: 形近组与 conservative 读音相近，近义组列出与谨慎或传统相关的说法。

entries.definition: the protection of nature or resources
the belief in tradition and slow change
entries.definitionCN: 重视传统与缓变的信念

entries.definition: a glass building for plants or a music school
following long-established customs
careful to avoid risk
favouring tradition and free markets
entries.definitionCN: 倾向传统与自由市场的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from an old chair kept in a new room, then move to a cautious view and to a number said low on purpose.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从新房间里那张旧椅子开始，再到谨慎的看法，最后到故意说低的数字。

normal.en: Con- is together and serv- is keep, so a conservative person keeps things as they are.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，serv- 是保存，conservative 的人就是要把东西保持原样。

normal.en: The old chair is ugly and comfortable; comfort wins.
normal.cn: 旧椅子难看却舒服，而舒服赢了。

normal.en: A conservative estimate is a promise said quietly.
normal.cn: 保守的估计，是把承诺轻声说出来。

normal.en: Slow change is not no change, only change with brakes.
normal.cn: 缓慢的改变不是不改变，而是带着刹车的改变。

normal.en: When in doubt, choose the door that already opens.
normal.cn: 拿不准的时候，选那扇本来就能打开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a new room with one old chair in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一间新屋子，中间只摆着一把旧椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand placed flat on a table to steady it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平按在桌上把桌子稳住。

abstract.en: Picture a number written small, then circled twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写得很小的数字，被圈了两道。

examples.en: He gave a conservative estimate of the cost.
examples.cn: 他对费用给出了一个偏低的估计。

examples.en: Her parents are conservative about marriage.
examples.cn: 她父母对婚姻的看法比较保守。

examples.en: The plan is conservative, but it will not fail.
examples.cn: 这个方案偏保守，但不会失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conservative 记成 conserve（保存）加 ative：凡事想着先保存旧样子，就是保守；说数字也先往低处放。

root: 源自拉丁语 conservare（com 一起 + servare 保存），本义是有保存作用的，后指守旧、谨慎与偏低估计。

sensesIntro.en: From keeping an old chair, to a cautious view of the market, and finally to a number deliberately set low.
sensesIntro.cn: 从留住一把旧椅子，到对市场的谨慎看法，最后到故意说低的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old chair kept in the middle of a new room.
core.cn: 核心意象：新屋子中间留着一把旧椅子。

branches.en: The first sense is a taste for what already works.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是偏爱已经管用的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is caution about risk.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是对风险的谨慎。

branches.en: The third sense puts caution into a number.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把谨慎放进一个数字里。

branches.en: Loving the old and fearing risk pull in the same direction.
branches.cn: 偏爱旧物与畏惧风险，朝同一个方向拉。

branches.en: A cautious mind writes a low estimate and sleeps well.
branches.cn: 谨慎的人写下偏低的估计，然后睡得安稳。

intro.en: Conservative is built on Latin conservare, from com-, together, and servare, to keep.
intro.cn: conservative 由拉丁语 conservare 构成，源头是 com-（一起）与 servare（保存）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin keep base serv- also appears in preserve, reserve and observe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的保存词基 serv- 也出现在 preserve、reserve 与 observe 中。

items.meaning: belief in tradition and slow change
items.meaningCN: 重视传统与缓变的信念
items.exampleCN: 他的保守倾向随年龄增长。
注意观察这台机器如何运转。

definition_en: an instrument that shows direction, a tool for drawing circles, or the range of something
core_image: 掌心大小的圆盘上，一根磁针轻轻摆动后定住指向北方
scene: 山里起雾，队长掏出小圆盘看指针方向。 Without a compass they would have walked in circles.
sceneCN: 这里 compass 指「指南针」（第 1 个义项：指示方向的仪器）；句意是没有指南针，他们就会原地绕圈。

derivatives.zh: 包含；包围
圆规；罗盘
罗盘方位图
罗盘方位

senses.title: The direction finder
senses.definition: an instrument with a magnetic needle that always points north
senses.definitionCN: 带磁针、始终指向北方的仪器
senses.example: The compass swung and settled on north.
senses.exampleCN: 罗盘转了转，停在了北面。
senses.why: A needle that finds north gives the traveller the one fixed line everything else is measured from.
senses.whyCN: 找到北方的磁针给了旅人一条固定线，其余方向都由它量出。

senses.title: The drawing tool
senses.definition: a tool with two legs used for drawing circles
senses.definitionCN: 用来画圆的两脚工具
senses.example: He drew a perfect circle with a compass.
senses.exampleCN: 他用圆规画了一个完美的圆。
senses.why: Both meanings turn on measuring a circle or a round world, so they share one name.
senses.whyCN: 两个义项都围绕测量圆或圆形世界，所以共用一个名字。

senses.title: The range or scope
senses.definition: the limit or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的限度或范围
senses.example: Such a journey lies beyond the compass of one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的旅程超出了一个夏天的范围。
senses.why: A compass marks how far a circle reaches, so it came to mean any reach or limit.
senses.whyCN: 罗盘标出圆能伸到多远，于是引申为任何范围或限度。

intro.en: Compass comes from Latin com, together, and passus, a step, and first meant to pace out a circle of ground.
intro.cn: compass 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（一步），本义是按步量出一圈地面。

items.en: Passus was the length of one step.
items.cn: passus 指一步的长度。

items.en: Compassare meant to measure a space by walking round it.
items.cn: compassare 意为绕着走一圈来量一块地方。

items.en: Old French compasser kept the sense of going round.
items.cn: 古法语 compasser 保留了绕行一圈的意思。

items.en: English compass first named a circuit or a boundary.
items.cn: 英语 compass 最初指一圈或一条边界。

items.en: It moved to the needle for direction, the tool for circles and any scope.
items.cn: 后来它转向指方向的磁针、画圆的工具以及任何范围。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words with a similar sound or shape, and the meaning group names other words for direction, range and guidance.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音或形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示方向、范围与指引的词。

entries.definition: decayed plant material used to enrich soil
to press something into a smaller space
the grounds of a university
the range of a subject or activity
the limits within which something works
something that shows the way

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a needle settling on north, then move to the tool that draws circles and to any reach or limit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从磁针定在北方开始，再走到画圆的工具以及任何范围或限度。

normal.en: Com- is together and pass means step, so a compass measures a walk in a circle.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pass 是步子，所以 compass 量的是绕一圈的路。

normal.en: One needle, one fixed north: that is why a compass calms a lost walker.
normal.cn: 一根磁针，一个固定的北方：所以罗盘能让迷路的人安心。

normal.en: Two legs and a point draw a perfect circle.
normal.cn: 两条腿加一个尖点，就能画出完美的圆。

normal.en: The compass of a book is the range it covers.
normal.cn: 一本书的 compass 就是它覆盖的范围。

normal.en: En- plus compass gives encompass, to go all the way round.
normal.cn: en- 加 compass 得到 encompass，意为整个围起来。

abstract.en: Picture a needle trembling, then holding still on north.
abstract.cn: 想象磁针抖了几下，然后定在北方不动。

abstract.en: Picture a metal point pressed into paper, a circle opening out.
abstract.cn: 想象金属尖压进纸里，一个圆慢慢张开。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that marks how far the land goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，标出土地延伸到哪里。

examples.en: The compass needle pointed steadily north.
examples.cn: 指南针的指针稳稳地指向北方。

examples.en: Draw the circle with a compass and a pencil.
examples.cn: 用圆规和铅笔画这个圆。

examples.en: That subject lies beyond the compass of this book.
examples.cn: 那个题目超出了本书的范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compass 记成 com（一起）加 pass（步）：一起量步、绕行一圈，圆盘定方向，两脚画圆，也都量出范围。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（步），本义是按步量地、绕行一圈，后指量圆的工具与指示方向的罗盘，再引申为范围。

sensesIntro.en: From a needle that finds north, to a tool that draws the round world, and finally to any reach or limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从找到北方的磁针，到画圆的工具，最后到任何范围或限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm-sized dial whose needle trembles, then holds on north.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心大小的圆盘上，一根磁针轻轻摆动后定住指向北方。

branches.en: Finding north is the sense travellers cling to.
branches.cn: 找到北方是旅人最依赖的义项。

branches.en: The drawing tool keeps the old idea of a measured circle.
branches.cn: 画圆工具保留了量出一个圆的古老想法。

branches.en: Any boundary is a circle drawn around a thing.
branches.cn: 任何边界都是围绕某物画出的一圈。

branches.en: A needle gives direction, and a boundary gives range.
branches.cn: 磁针给方向，边界给范围。

branches.en: Both senses come from one act: measuring a round space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出自同一个动作：量出一块圆的范围。

intro.en: Compass is built on Latin com, together, plus passus, a step.
intro.cn: compass 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 passus（一步）构成。

latinIntro.en: The step base pass- also appears in passage and in bypass.
latinIntro.cn: 表示步子的词基 pass- 也出现在 passage 与 bypass 里。

items.meaning: the drawing tool with two legs
items.example: A pair of compasses sat on the desk.
The course encompasses both theory and practice.
items.exampleCN: 这门课包含理论与实践。
这个计划包含三个阶段。

items.example: She has an encompassing view of the field.
items.exampleCN: 她对这一领域有全局的视野。

items.example: The old walls encompassed the whole town.
items.exampleCN: 旧城墙围住了整个镇子。

items.meaning: one of the main directions on a compass
items.example: North is the first compass point we learn.
items.exampleCN: 北是我们最先学的罗盘方位。

items.meaning: the printed star of directions on a map
items.example: The map shows a small compass rose.
items.exampleCN: 地图上画着一个小罗盘方位图。

items.example: The ship was compassing the island.

definition_zh: 摩托车；骑摩托车；（作定语）摩托车的
definition_en: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine that one or two people ride; also used before a noun for equipment, races or police work connected with such vehicles; and as a verb meaning to travel on one
core_image: 两个轮子夹着一台发动机，排气管在暮色里吐出一缕白烟
scene: 黄昏的海岸路上，年轻人把头盔扣紧，发动机的声音压过了风声。 He rode his motorcycle along the cliffs until the last light faded.
sceneCN: 这里「motorcycle」是「摩托车」（第 1 个义项：有发动机的两轮车）；句意为他骑着摩托车沿悬崖一路走，直到最后一点光也暗下去。画面里能想见：扣紧的头盔、海岸公路与崖边的暮色。

collocations.zh: 骑摩托的警察；摩托警队

derivatives.zh: 由 motorcycle 去掉词尾再加 -ist 构成，义为「骑摩托车的人」
由 motorcycle 去掉词尾再加 -ing 构成，义为「摩托车运动；骑摩托车」
由 motor 与 bike 缩合而成，义为「摩托车」，与 motorcycle 近义
由 motor 加 -cade（借自 cavalcade 的词尾）构成，义为「机动车辆组成的车队」

senses.title: A two-wheeled vehicle powered by an engine
senses.definition: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine that one or two people ride
senses.definitionCN: 一种有两个轮子、由发动机驱动的路上交通工具，可载一两个人
senses.example: She parked her motorcycle under the mango tree.
senses.exampleCN: 她把摩托车停在芒果树下。
senses.why: The word is a plain English compound: motor supplies the engine and cycle supplies the wheel, so the name simply describes the machine's two working parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是直白的英语复合词：motor 提供发动机，cycle 提供轮子，名字本身就在描述这台机器的两个工作部件。

senses.title: Used before a noun for things connected with motorcycles
senses.titleCN: （作定语）摩托车的；供摩托车使用的
senses.definition: placed before another noun to describe equipment, clothing, races or police work that belongs to motorcycles
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，说明某装备、服装、赛事或警务与摩托车有关
senses.example: A row of motorcycle police waited at the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一队骑摩托的警察在桥边等着。
senses.why: A common noun that names a vehicle easily becomes a label for everything built around it, so helmets, races and patrols simply borrow the vehicle's name.
senses.whyCN: 一个指交通工具的普通名词，很容易变成围绕它的一切事物的标签，于是头盔、比赛和巡逻都直接借用了这辆车的名字。

senses.title: To ride a motorcycle
senses.definition: to travel on a motorcycle, usually as the person steering it
senses.definitionCN: 骑摩托车出行，通常指掌握车把的那个人
senses.example: They motorcycled across the island in three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用三天时间骑摩托环游了这座岛。
senses.why: English often turns a vehicle noun into a verb without adding any ending, so the machine's name also names the act of using it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个交通工具名词原样变成动词，于是这台机器的名字同时也指使用它的那个动作。

intro.en: Motorcycle is not a Latin word but a nineteenth-century English compound of two borrowed parts, one for motion and one for the wheel.
intro.cn: motorcycle 不是拉丁词，而是十九世纪英语用两个借来的成分拼成的复合词：一个表示运动，一个表示轮子。

items.en: Kyklos meant a circle or a wheel, and Greek writers used it for anything round, including the wheel of a cart.
items.cn: kyklos 意为圆或轮子，古希腊作家用它指一切圆形之物，包括马车的车轮。

items.en: Latin borrowed kyklos as cyclus and passed the wheel idea into learned English through French forms of cycle.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 kyklos 作 cyclus，又把「轮子」的观念经法语中的 cycle 形式带入学术英语。

items.en: Movere meant to move; its derived noun motor named the thing that gives motion, a term later applied to an engine.
items.cn: movere 意为移动；由它派生的名词 motor 指「使动者」，后来用来指发动机。

items.en: Late nineteenth-century English joined motor and cycle to name engine-driven two-wheelers, at first often written as two words.
items.cn: 十九世纪晚期英语把 motor 与 cycle 合起来指发动机驱动的两轮车，起初常分写成两个词。

items.en: Modern English spells the compound as one word and extends it to motorcycle police, motorcycle racing and the verb to motorcycle.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词连写成一个词，并扩展到摩托警队、摩托车比赛以及动词「骑摩托车」。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the compound and words built on them; the near-meaning group gathers small powered two-wheelers.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个复合词的两半以及建立在它们之上的词展开；近义组收表示小型动力两轮车的词。

entries.definition: The half of the word that supplies the engine and the idea of motion.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中提供发动机与运动观念的那一半。

entries.definition: A person who drives a car, built on the same motor stem.
entries.definitionCN: 开车的人，建立在同一个 motor 词干上。

entries.definition: The wheel word inside motorcycle, also used for bicycles and repeated rounds.
entries.definitionCN: motorcycle 里表示轮子的那个词，也用于自行车与循环。

entries.definition: A procession of motor vehicles, from motor plus the ending of cavalcade.
entries.definitionCN: 由机动车辆组成的车队，由 motor 加 cavalcade 的词尾构成。

entries.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle driven by pedals, sharing the cycle part.
entries.definitionCN: 靠脚踏驱动的两轮车，与 motorcycle 共用 cycle 这一部分。

entries.definition: A motorcycle, especially a small or light one, in informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 摩托车，尤指小型轻便的，英式口语用法。

entries.definition: A small motorcycle with a frame you can step through.
entries.definitionCN: 车架可跨步上下的小型摩托车；踏板车。

entries.definition: A light two-wheeled vehicle with a small engine and pedals.
entries.definitionCN: 装有小型发动机和脚踏板的轻型两轮车。

entries.definition: A bicycle or, informally, a motorcycle.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车，口语中也指摩托车。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound with a moving half and a wheel half, and its family keeps circling engines, riders and the roads they use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「动力」与「轮子」两半合成，词族反复围着发动机、骑手和他们走的路转。

normal.en: Motor is the moving part of the name and cycle is the wheel part, so the compound reads almost like a label fixed to the machine.
normal.cn: motor 是名字里「动力」的部分，cycle 是「轮子」的部分，这个复合词读起来几乎像贴在机器上的标签。

normal.en: Motorcyclist swaps the final -e for -ist, the way a person who does something often takes that ending.
normal.cn: motorcyclist 把词尾的 -e 换成 -ist，就像做某事的人常用这个后缀来称呼自己。

normal.en: Motorcycling adds -ing: the activity built around the vehicle.
normal.cn: motorcycling 加 -ing：围绕这辆车展开的活动。

normal.en: Bicycle already joins bi- (two) with cycle, so motorcycle uses the same wheel word with a different first half.
normal.cn: bicycle 已经把 bi-（两个）和 cycle 连在一起，所以 motorcycle 用的是同一个「轮」词，只换了前半截。

normal.en: The noun also works as a verb without any ending, as in 「they motorcycled across the island」.
normal.cn: 这个名词不加词尾也能当动词用，例如「他们骑摩托环游全岛」。

abstract.en: A name made of two borrowed parts reminds us that new machines are often labelled with old words for motion and wheels.
abstract.cn: 由两个借来的成分拼成的名字提醒人：新机器常常用表示运动与轮子的旧词来命名。

abstract.en: The same noun can name the vehicle, its accessories and the ride, because English lets a thing's name spread to everything around it.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词可以指车、指配件、也指骑行本身，因为英语允许一件东西的名字蔓延到它周围的一切。

abstract.en: Two wheels and an engine turn a person into a rider, and the word carries that small transformation inside it.
abstract.cn: 两个轮子加一台发动机，把人变成骑手，而这个词把这场小小的转变装在里面。

examples.en: He rode his motorcycle along the cliffs until the last light faded.
examples.cn: 他骑着摩托车沿悬崖一路走，直到最后一点光也暗下去。

examples.en: A row of motorcycle police waited at the bridge.
examples.cn: 一队骑摩托的警察在桥边等着。

examples.en: She saved for two years before buying her first motorcycle.
examples.cn: 她攒了两年的钱，才买下第一辆摩托车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托」——汉语把 motor 音译成「摩托」，再加两个轮子，就是摩托车。

root: motorcycle 是十九世纪英语的复合词，由 motor（源自拉丁语 movere，意为「移动」）与 cycle（源自希腊语 kyklos，意为「圆、轮」）拼合而成，整词层面没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an engine joined to two wheels; the senses name the machine itself, its attributive use as a label, and the act of riding it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一台发动机接上两个轮子；义项分别指这台机器本身、它作定语的标签用法，以及骑它的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two wheels with an engine between them, a thin trail of smoke in the dusk.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个轮子中间夹一台发动机，暮色里拖出一缕细烟。

branches.en: a rider tightening a helmet strap at dusk
branches.cn: 暮色中骑手扣紧头盔带子

branches.en: a row of police machines waiting at a bridge
branches.cn: 桥边排开的警用摩托

branches.en: a race banner stretched over a coastal road
branches.cn: 横跨海岸公路的比赛横幅

branches.en: a machine leaning into a long bend
branches.cn: 一辆在长弯里倾斜而过的摩托

branches.en: a tank filled at a roadside station
branches.cn: 在路边加油站加满油

intro.en: Two borrowed halves, an engine word and a wheel word, are held together by English compounding and a handful of endings.
intro.cn: 两个借来的成分——一个引擎词和一个轮子词——由英语复合构词法和几个词尾连接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Movere, motor and cyclus are recorded Latin forms and they supply the two halves of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: movere、motor 与 cyclus 是有记录的拉丁词形，为这个复合词的两半提供来源。

items.meaning: one who or that which does

latinEntries.meaning: a mover, one that imparts motion

definition_zh: 折磨；酷刑；拷打；极度痛苦；使受折磨
definition_en: the act of causing severe pain to punish or force a confession, or great mental suffering
core_image: 绳索被绞紧，一具身体在绳子另一端绷得笔直
scene: 牙科诊室外的长椅上，患者捏着挂号单，听见里面机器的声音就皱起眉。 Waiting three hours for a reply was pure torture.
sceneCN: 这里 torture 是精神上的「折磨」（第 2 个义项：极度的痛苦煎熬）；句意为等回信的三个小时简直是纯粹的折磨。画面里有诊室外的长椅、捏紧的单子与紧锁的眉。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受折磨的；（文体）矫揉的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「施酷刑者」
加 -ous 构成，义为「折磨人的；曲折痛苦的」
同根形容词，义为「曲折的；拐弯抹角的」

senses.title: The deliberate infliction of pain
senses.definition: the act of causing severe physical pain to a person, often to punish or to extract information
senses.definitionCN: 为使某人受罚或招供而故意造成剧烈肉体痛苦的行为
senses.example: The treaty forbids torture under any circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止在任何情况下使用酷刑。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest one in English, and international law still uses the word in exactly this way.
senses.whyCN: 这个法律义项是英语里最早出现的，国际法至今仍按这一含义使用该词。

senses.title: Severe mental suffering
senses.definition: great suffering of the mind, caused by worry, guilt, or waiting
senses.definitionCN: 由忧虑、内疚或等待造成的巨大精神痛苦
senses.example: The weeks before the results came out were torture for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布前的几周对全家都是折磨。
senses.why: Pain that is not physical still feels inflicted, so the old word for bodily torment moves into the mind.
senses.whyCN: 非身体的痛苦仍像是被人施加的，于是那个老旧的肉体折磨之词转入了心灵。

senses.title: Something that causes suffering
senses.definition: a thing or situation that is extremely unpleasant to endure
senses.definitionCN: 极难忍受的事物或处境
senses.example: That traffic on Friday evenings is absolute torture.
senses.exampleCN: 周五傍晚的那段交通简直是折磨。
senses.why: Everyday things that cannot be escaped often take the strongest available word, and this is one of the strongest.
senses.whyCN: 无法逃避的日常之事常借用手上最强的词，而这正是一个很强的词。

senses.title: To cause pain to someone
senses.definition: to inflict pain on a person, physically or mentally
senses.definitionCN: 在肉体或精神上给某人造成痛苦
senses.example: He was tortured by doubt for months before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 决定之前，他被疑虑折磨了好几个月。
senses.why: The verb allows both a physical agent and an abstract one, which is why doubt can torture a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可接实在的施动者，也可接抽象者，所以「疑虑」也能折磨一个人。

senses.title: To twist the meaning of words
senses.definition: to force a word or idea into a sense it does not naturally carry
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词或观念硬扭成它本来没有的意思
senses.example: Do not torture the sentence into meaning the opposite of what it says.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把这个句子曲解成与它原意相反的意思。
senses.why: Meaning can be bent out of shape as a body can, which brings the word back to its twisting root.
senses.whyCN: 意义可以像身体一样被扭得变形，这又把这个词带回它「扭」的词根。

senses.title: The historical instrument of law
senses.definition: the use of pain as a legal instrument in past legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 过去法律体系中把疼痛当作法律手段的做法
senses.example: Records show that torture was used to obtain confessions in that court.
senses.exampleCN: 档案显示那个法庭曾用刑讯逼取口供。
senses.why: In legal history the word names an admitted procedure, which is what makes it valuable in reading old records.
senses.whyCN: 在法律史上这个词曾指一种被承认的程序，读旧档案时正因如此才需要它。

senses.title: The writer's strained style
senses.definition: in the phrase tortured style, language that is forced and unnatural
senses.definitionCN: 在 tortured style 这一说法中，指勉强而不自然的文笔
senses.example: The translation reads in a tortured style that hides the plain sense.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文文笔矫揉，把明白的意思藏了起来。
senses.why: Style that is forced is like a rope pulled too far, so the same adjective serves both pain and prose.
senses.whyCN: 强扭的文风就像拉得太过的绳，于是同一个形容词兼用于痛苦与文笔。

senses.title: The metaphor of the twisted rope
senses.definition: the underlying image of something twisted out of its natural shape
senses.definitionCN: 底层意象是某物被扭离其自然形态
senses.example: The road tortures itself around the mountain through a dozen hairpins.
senses.exampleCN: 那条路绕山拐了十几个急弯。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical image in the background, while the adjective tortuous shows it plainly.
senses.whyCN: 名词把物理意象留在背景里，而形容词 tortuous 把它明明白白地呈现出来。

intro.en: Torture comes from Latin tortura, a twisting, from torquere, to twist; the sense moved from bending the body out of shape to pain inflicted on purpose.
intro.cn: torture 来自拉丁语 tortura（扭绞），源于 torquere（扭）；其义从把身体扭得变形，转到故意施加的痛苦。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or bend, and tortura is a twisting, used of ropes under strain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭、弯，tortura 是扭绞本身，用于受力的绳索。

items.en: In legal Latin tortura names the application of force to make a person speak.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语中，tortura 指施加暴力以逼人开口。

items.en: Old French torture carries the legal sense of judicial tormentation into medieval courts.
items.cn: 古法语 torture 把司法拷问的法律含义带入中世纪法庭。

items.en: English borrows torture in the fifteenth century, first as a legal term and then more widely.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 torture，先作为法律术语，后扩展到更广的用法。

items.en: The mental sense, as in the torture of waiting, becomes common in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 「等待的折磨」这类精神意义在十八世纪普遍起来。

items.en: The older physical image survives in tortuous, the adjective for a winding road, and in the mechanics of torque.
items.cn: 古老的物理意象保存在 tortuous（形容蜿蜒之路）与力学中的 torque 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the twisting-root relatives, while the near-meaning group gathers words for suffering and for cruelty.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一「扭绞」词根的亲属词，近义组则汇集表示痛苦与残暴的词。

entries.definition: full of twists and turns, or devious
a person who inflicts torture
causing great pain
a twisting force
extreme pain of body or mind
the state of undergoing pain
great suffering, or a cause of it
ease and relief from pain

normalIntro.en: These memories use the twisting root shared with torque and tortuous, the two senses of body and mind, and the phrase be tortured by.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用与 torque、tortuous 共有的「扭绞」词根、身心两个义项，以及 be tortured by 这一搭配。

normal.en: The root is twist, so torture is a body or a mind twisted out of its shape.
normal.cn: 词根是「扭」，所以折磨就是把身体或心思扭得变形。

normal.en: Torture, torque, and tortuous share the twist, and their meanings tell you which way it went.
normal.cn: torture、torque、tortuous 共用「扭」，各自的含义说明它扭向了哪边。

normal.en: Be tortured by doubt is the common passive pattern for the mental sense.
normal.cn: be tortured by doubt 是精神义常用的被动态。

normal.en: Sheer torture and mental torture both take the noun as an uncountable mass.
normal.cn: sheer torture 与 mental torture 都把名词当作不可数的整体。

normal.en: Tortured style means forced writing, which is the same twist applied to language.
normal.cn: tortured style 指矫揉的文笔，就是把同样的扭力施加到语言上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight until it hums, and then pulled further.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳被拉紧到发出嗡声，然后又被拉。

abstract.en: Think of a clock face you cannot stop watching while you wait for news.
abstract.cn: 想一张你等消息时无法不看的钟面。

abstract.en: Torture is imposed pain, and the word keeps the memory that it was once done with ropes.
abstract.cn: 酷刑是被施加的痛，这个词保存着它曾用绳索实施的记忆。

examples.en: The prisoners were held for weeks without charges or torture of any kind.
examples.cn: 这些被拘留者数周未受指控，也没有遭受任何形式的酷刑。

examples.en: He was tortured by the memory of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他被自己所说过的话的记忆折磨着。

examples.en: The long bus ride was torture for the children.
examples.cn: 漫长的长途汽车之旅对孩子们是种折磨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「同扯」——两人同扯一根绳，扯得生疼，就是折磨。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭、绞）→ tortura（扭绞；刑讯）→ 古法语 torture → 英语 torture。同根词有 torque、tortuous、tort。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the deliberate infliction of pain, then moves to the suffering that is not physical, to the verb of tormenting, and at last back to the twisting image that started it: twisted words, twisted roads, and twisted style.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从故意施加的痛苦写起，再到非身体的苦痛、表示折磨的动词，最后回到最初的「扭」这一意象：扭曲的词、蜿蜒的路与矫揉的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something pulled or twisted out of its natural shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉扯、扭离其自然形态之物。

branches.en: Pain inflicted deliberately, by law or by force.
branches.cn: 由法律或暴力故意施加的痛苦。

branches.en: Suffering of the mind and the things that cause it.
branches.cn: 精神苦痛及其来源。

branches.en: The verb of tormenting or being tormented.
branches.cn: 折磨或被折磨的动词用法。

branches.en: Meaning and style twisted out of shape.
branches.cn: 被扭曲的意义与文风。

branches.en: The rope image carried into roads and mechanics.
branches.cn: 绳索意象被带入道路与力学。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin twisting stem with -ura, and English adds -ed, -er, -ous, and the parallel -uous.
intro.cn: 本词由拉丁语「扭绞」词干加 -ura 构成，英语再加 -ed、-er、-ous 以及平行的 -uous。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the twisting verb, its noun, and the related noun for torment.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「扭绞」动词、其名词以及相关的「苦痛」名词。

items.example: The stem is the twisted body of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是这个词被扭过的主体。

items.example: Tortura is the act of twisting.
Torturer names the one who acts.
Tort is the legal cousin of the word.
items.exampleCN: tort 是本词的法律亲属。

items.example: Torment is the sister noun of suffering.
items.exampleCN: torment 是表示苦痛的姊妹名词。

definition_en: a very small living thing that can cause disease
core_image: 显微镜下一颗会游动的杆状小东西
scene: 实验室的镜片下出现一小片灰色。 A single bacterium can divide within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 bacterium 是「细菌」（第 1 个义项：极微小的单细胞生物）；句意是一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁复数形式，义为「细菌（复数）」
由 bacterium 加 -al 构成，义为「细菌的」
由 bacterio- 与 -logy 构成，义为「细菌学」

senses.title: A single microbe
senses.definition: a very small single-celled living thing, some of which cause disease
senses.definitionCN: 极微小的单细胞生物，有些会致病
senses.example: A single bacterium can divide within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。
senses.why: Bacterium is Latin for a little rod, the shape early microscopists saw, so the scientific name began as a description of form.
senses.whyCN: bacterium 在拉丁语中意为「小杆」，是早期显微镜观察者看到的形状，所以这个学名起初是对形态的描述。

senses.title: A cause of infection
senses.definition: a bacterium that infects the body and causes illness
senses.definitionCN: 侵入人体并引起疾病的细菌
senses.example: One bacterium was enough to spoil the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 一个细菌就足以让样本坏掉。
senses.why: Because some species cause disease, the singular often appears in medical writing about infection.
senses.whyCN: 由于某些种类会致病，单数形式常出现在讲感染的医学文字中。

intro.en: Bacterium is a scientific name taken from a Greek word for a rod.
intro.cn: bacterium 是一个取自希腊语「杆」的学名。

items.en: bakterion meant 'a small rod'.
items.cn: bakterion 意为「小杆」。

items.en: scientists used bacterium for rod-shaped microbes.
items.cn: 科学家用 bacterium 指杆状微生物。

items.en: English borrowed the singular form.
items.cn: 英语借入了这个单数形式。

items.en: the Latin plural became the everyday word.
items.cn: 拉丁复数成了日常使用的词。

items.en: Bacterium is now mainly scientific.
items.cn: 如今 bacterium 主要用于科学语境。

note.en: The look-alike group is the scientific family; the near-meaning group gives everyday words for tiny organisms.
note.cn: 形近组是科学词族；近义组是日常说法中的微小生物。

normal.cn: 复数是 bacteria，不是 bacteriums。

normal.en: The adjective is bacterial.
normal.cn: 形容词是 bacterial。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: bac-TE-ri-um.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: A bacterium is a single cell, so it is not visible to the eye.
normal.cn: 一个细菌只有一个细胞，所以肉眼看不见。

normal.en: Not every bacterium causes disease.
normal.cn: 并非每个细菌都会致病。

abstract.en: See a tiny rod swimming under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜片下一根游动的小杆。

abstract.en: See one dot splitting into two.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小点分裂成两个。

abstract.en: See a grey smear on a glass slide.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃载片上的一小片灰色。

examples.cn: 一个细菌几分钟内就能分裂。

examples.en: One bacterium was enough to spoil the sample.
examples.cn: 一个细菌就足以让样本坏掉。

examples.en: Each bacterium in the sample was counted.
examples.cn: 样本中的每一个细菌都被计数了。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin took the Greek diminutive and gave English the pair bacterium and bacteria.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁语借入这个希腊指小词，给英语留下 bacterium 与 bacteria 这对形式。

definition_en: in a way that shows deep pain or anger
core_image: 转身离开时绷紧的嘴角
scene: 她转过身，嘴角绷得发白。 She wept bitterly after the letter arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 bitterly 是「痛苦地」（第 1 个义项：带着深切痛苦的方式）；句意是信到之后她痛哭起来。

pos.zh: 副词：极其，用于修饰寒冷、失望等负面词

derivatives.zh: 苦味；痛苦；怨恨
使心怀怨恨，使处境更糟

senses.title: With deep pain
senses.definition: in a way that shows great sadness or suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出深切悲伤或痛苦的方式
senses.example: She wept bitterly after the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信到之后她痛哭起来。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turned the taste word into a way of showing pain.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把这个味道词变成了表现痛苦的方式。

senses.title: With strong resentment
senses.definition: in a way that shows anger and a sense of unfairness
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出愤怒与不公之感的方式
senses.example: He complained bitterly about the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他愤愤地抱怨那个决定。
senses.why: The anger sense of bitter passed straight into the adverb.
senses.whyCN: bitter 的怨恨义直接进入了副词。

senses.title: To an extreme degree
senses.definition: used with words like cold to mean very severely
senses.definitionCN: 与 cold 等词连用，表示程度极其严重
senses.example: It was bitterly cold on the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 站台上冷得刺骨。
senses.why: Bitter cold was so sharp that the adverb became a general intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 刺骨的寒冷太强烈，副词因而成了泛用的程度加强词。

intro.en: Bitterly is bitter plus the old adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: bitterly 是 bitter 加上古老的副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: biter meant sharp to the taste.
items.cn: biter 意为味道尖锐的。

items.en: the ending -lice formed adverbs from adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -lice 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: bitterliche became the modern bitterly.
items.cn: bitterliche 演变为今天的 bitterly。

items.en: bitterly described weeping and grief.
items.cn: bitterly 开始形容哭泣与悲伤。

items.en: bitterly also strengthens cold and disappointment.
items.cn: 如今 bitterly 也用来加强寒冷与失望的程度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -tterly shape; the near-meaning group gives other adverbs of intensity.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -tterly 的词形；近义组是其他表示程度的副词。

entries.definition: having a sharp unpleasant taste
a bitter drink used in cocktails
recently or lately
very much or severely
to a great degree
in a cruel or severe way

normalIntro.en: Bitterly tells how something bitter is done or felt.
normalIntro.cn: bitterly 说明一件苦事是以怎样的方式发生或被感受的。

normal.en: Add -ly to bitter to get the adverb.
normal.cn: bitter 加 -ly 就是副词。

normal.en: Weep bitterly is the most common pairing.
normal.cn: weep bitterly 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Bitterly cold means extremely cold.
normal.cn: bitterly cold 表示冷到极点。

normal.en: Complain bitterly shows lasting anger.
normal.cn: complain bitterly 显出积压的怒气。

normal.en: The adverb never changes form.
normal.cn: 这个副词形式从不变化。

abstract.en: See a letter held in shaking hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被颤抖的手捏着。

abstract.en: See someone arguing with a tight jaw.
abstract.cn: 想象有人绷着下巴争辩。

abstract.en: See breath turning white on a frozen platform.
abstract.cn: 想象在冰冷的站台上呼出白气。

examples.en: She wept bitterly after the letter arrived.
examples.cn: 信到之后她痛哭起来。

examples.en: He complained bitterly about the decision.
examples.cn: 他愤愤地抱怨那个决定。

examples.en: It was bitterly cold on the platform.
examples.cn: 站台上冷得刺骨。

dict_mnemonic.text: bitter 是苦，ly 是副词尾巴，苦到心里，就成了痛苦地、怨恨地。

root: bitterly 由形容词 bitter 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，-ly 源自古英语 -lice；本义「带苦味地」，中古英语起引申为痛苦地、怨恨地，并常与 cold 连用表示严寒。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb carries grief, resentment and biting cold.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词同时承载悲苦、怨恨与刺骨的严寒。

intro.cn: bitterly 是规则的 -ly 副词，拼写遵循清楚的规则。
