latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_en: a weapon that flies through the air to hit a distant target, or, in older use, any object thrown or fired
core_image: 一道白线划破天空，拐了个弯追向远处的靶
scene: 试验场的雷达屏幕亮着，远处拖出一道白线。 Operators watched the missile bank in mid-air and follow the target drone across the sky.
sceneCN: 这里是「导弹」（第 1 个义项：可制导的远程武器）；句意为操作员看着导弹在空中转弯，追着靶机划过天空。图中可辨识物件：雷达屏幕、白线、靶机。

derivatives.zh: 由 missile 加表示「人」的 -eer 构成，指从事导弹工作或操作导弹的人
由 missile 加 -ry 构成，指导弹的总称或导弹技术
由 anti-（反）与 missile 复合而成，指用于拦截导弹的

senses.title: A guided weapon that flies to a distant target
senses.definition: a weapon, usually rocket-powered, that is launched and then guided through the air to hit a distant target
senses.definitionCN: 一种通常由火箭推进的武器，发射后可被引导飞向远处目标
senses.example: The defence system tracked the incoming missile from the moment it left the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 防御系统从导弹离地那一刻起就跟踪着它。
senses.why: Latin missile first meant any object thrown; once engineers could steer that object while it flew, the old word for a thrown thing took on the modern sense of a guided weapon.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 missile 本指任何被投出的东西；当工程师能让飞行中的物体改变方向，这个「投出去的东西」就顺势成了能被引导的现代武器。

senses.title: An object thrown by hand as a weapon
senses.definition: a stone, spear or other object thrown by hand to strike someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用手投出去、用来击打人或物的石头、长矛等物体
senses.example: The crowd threw stones and other missiles at the soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 人群朝士兵投掷石块和其他投掷物。
senses.why: Before engines existed, the only way to send a blow across a distance was to throw something, and the Latin noun named exactly that object in the air.
senses.whyCN: 在有发动机之前，要把打击送到远处，只能靠手把东西扔出去；拉丁语名词指的正是空中那件被投出的物体，这是最贴近字面的一层。

senses.title: A projectile fired from a gun or cannon
senses.definition: a shell, bullet or similar projectile fired from a gun or cannon rather than thrown by hand
senses.definitionCN: 由枪炮射出而非用手投出的炮弹、子弹之类
senses.example: Old gunnery manuals list the weight of every missile the battery could fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的火炮手册会列出炮组能射出的每一种弹丸的重量。
senses.why: Gunpowder replaced the arm but not the idea: the object still leaves a hand or a barrel and flies to a target, so the same word stretched from stones to shells.
senses.whyCN: 火药换了手臂的位置，却换不掉那个念头：物体仍要从手里或炮口飞向目标，于是同一个词从石头一路盖到了炮弹。

intro.en: Missile comes straight from Latin, where it named any object thrown; English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century and later applied it to self-propelled weapons.
intro.cn: missile 直接来自拉丁语，本指任何被投出的物体；英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，后来才用它指自推进的武器。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, let go or throw, and its supine missum supplied the stem for a whole family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开、投掷，它的动名词形式 missum 为整整一族「送」的词提供了词干。

items.en: The adjective missilis meant that may be thrown, formed from the same stem with the suffix -ilis.
items.cn: 形容词 missilis 意为「可以被投出的」，由同一词干加后缀 -ilis 构成。

items.en: The neuter noun missile meant a thing thrown, whether a stone, a spear or a bolt.
items.cn: 中性名词 missile 指被投出的东西，可以是石头、长矛或弩箭。

items.en: English took the Latin noun in the seventeenth century, first for thrown objects and later for projectiles fired from guns.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入这个拉丁名词，先指被投掷的物体，后来也指枪炮射出的弹丸。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word narrowed onto rocket-powered weapons that steer in flight, while the older sense survives in historical writing.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词收窄到指飞行中可自行导向的火箭武器，较旧的含义则留在历史叙述里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Latin relatives and one derived person noun; the near-meaning group gathers flying weapons and the parts or payloads that travel with them.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁同族词与一个派生的人物名词；近义组收飞行武器以及随它一起飞行的部件或载荷。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective meaning able to be thrown, the direct source of missile.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语形容词，意为「可以被投出的」，正是 missile 的直接来源。

entries.definition: A task or a sending out, formed from the same Latin verb mittere.
entries.definitionCN: 任务或一次派遣，来自同一个拉丁动词 mittere。

entries.definition: To send someone away, built from dis- plus mittere.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人打发走，由 dis- 加 mittere 构成。

entries.definition: A person who works with or operates missiles.
entries.definitionCN: 从事导弹工作或操作导弹的人。

entries.definition: A vehicle driven by burning fuel and used to carry a warhead or a spacecraft.
entries.definitionCN: 靠燃烧燃料推进的飞行器，用来运送弹头或航天器。

entries.definition: Any object moving through the air after being thrown or fired.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被抛出或射出后在空中飞行的物体。

entries.definition: A self-propelled weapon that travels underwater toward a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 一种在水下自行推进、冲向舰船的武器。

entries.definition: The part of a missile that carries the explosive or the payload.
entries.definitionCN: 导弹中装载炸药或有效载荷的部分。

normalIntro.en: Latin mittere meant to send, and every relative of this word is about something or someone being sent.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送出」，这个词的同族词都在说某物或某人被送出去。

normal.en: Mittere meant to send, and missile is literally the thing sent.
normal.cn: mittere 意为「送出」，missile 字面就是「被送出的东西」。

normal.en: Missilis was the adjective for throwable, so the noun began in the air as a stone or a spear, not in a silo.
normal.cn: missilis 是「可投掷的」形容词，所以这个名词最早是在空中的石头或长矛，而不是在发射井里。

normal.en: Mission and dismiss share the same verb, one a sending out and one a sending away.
normal.cn: mission 与 dismiss 共用同一个动词，一个是派出去，一个是打发走。

normal.en: The modern weapon keeps the old grammar: something is still sent toward a target, only now it can steer.
normal.cn: 现代武器沿用旧的语法：仍有东西被送向目标，只是现在它能自己转向。

normal.en: Warhead, booster and guidance describe parts, while missile itself claims only that the object is thrown.
normal.cn: 弹头、助推器与制导描述的是零件，而 missile 本身只声明「这个物体是被投出去的」。

abstract.en: Every missile is a sentence in the oldest grammar of distance: I send this toward you.
abstract.cn: 每一枚导弹都在用最古老的「距离语法」说话：我把这个送向你。

abstract.en: The word stayed the same while the thrower changed from an arm to a rocket, which is how language survives technology.
abstract.cn: 投掷者从手臂换成火箭，词却没有变，语言就是这样熬过技术的更替。

abstract.en: A weapon named for throwing reminds us that the noun describes motion, not moral weight.
abstract.cn: 一个以「投掷」命名的武器提醒人：这个词描述的是运动，不是道德重量。

examples.en: The missile climbed steeply and then levelled off toward the coast.
examples.cn: 导弹陡直爬升，随后改平飞向海岸。

examples.en: A single missile can carry several warheads.
examples.cn: 一枚导弹可以携带多个弹头。

examples.en: The old manual still called a stone a missile.
examples.cn: 那本旧手册仍把石头称作投掷物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米赛尔」——像一支点火的箭在赛跑，一路冲向远方目标。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送出、投掷）的词干 miss- 加形容词后缀 -ilis 得 missilis（可投掷的），其中性名词 missile 指「被投出之物」；十七世纪进入英语，二十世纪专指可制导的导弹。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is a modern guided weapon; the other two keep the older meaning of any object sent through the air, whether by hand or by gunpowder.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项是现代的可制导武器；另外两个保留较旧的含义——任何被送过空中的物体，无论靠手还是靠火药。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white trail bending across the sky toward a far target.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道白线划破天空，拐了个弯追向远处的靶。

branches.en: a white trail bending in the sky toward a drone
branches.cn: 天空里一道转弯的白线追向靶机

branches.en: a stone leaving a hand and finding a shield
branches.cn: 石头离开手，撞上盾牌

branches.en: a cannon barrel flashing above a fortress wall
branches.cn: 炮口在城墙上方一闪

branches.en: a word for a thrown thing surviving into the rocket age
branches.cn: 「投出之物」的说法一路活到火箭时代

branches.en: one crew counting shells and another counting rockets
branches.cn: 一班人数炮弹，另一班人数火箭

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of sending, built from a verb, its supine stem and an adjective suffix, plus English relatives that kept the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「送」的名词，由一个动词、它的动名词词干和一个形容词后缀构成，再加上沿用同一词干的英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere and its supine missum are the direct source, and the Latin adjective missilis supplies the ending -ilis that marks something as throwable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 及其动名词 missum 是直接来源，拉丁形容词 missilis 则提供了表示「可以被投掷」的后缀 -ilis。

items.meaning: a weapon that flies to a target

definition_en: a person whose job is to amuse an audience
core_image: 舞台灯亮起，一个人向前一步，把全场的目光和笑声握在手里
scene: 游轮上那位唱歌的表演者每晚都要连唱两场。 The entertainer on the cruise ship sings two shows every night.
sceneCN: 这里 entertainer 是「表演者」（第 1 个义项：以娱乐观众为职业的人）；句意：游轮上的那位表演者每晚要唱两场。

derivatives.zh: 使娱乐；招待
娱乐；消遣
有趣的；令人愉快的

senses.title: A performer who amuses audiences
senses.definition: a person whose job is to entertain people, especially on stage or screen
senses.definitionCN: 以娱乐他人为职业的人，尤指在舞台或屏幕上
senses.example: The entertainer kept the whole room laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 这位表演者让整个房间笑声不断。
senses.why: The -er suffix names the person who carries out the action of entertaining.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 指执行 entertain 这一动作的人。

senses.title: A host who looks after guests
senses.definition: a person who is good at receiving and amusing guests
senses.definitionCN: 善于接待并逗客人开心的人
senses.example: As a host, she was a natural entertainer.
senses.exampleCN: 作为主人，她天生善于待客。
senses.why: The older hospitality sense of the verb produces this social meaning of the person.
senses.whyCN: 动词古老的「待客」义项，产生了这个指人的社交含义。

senses.title: A charming social person
senses.definition: someone who is lively and good at amusing people in company
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中活泼、善于逗乐的人
senses.example: He is a born entertainer, always at the centre of the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他天生会活跃气氛，总是聚会中的中心。
senses.why: Someone who holds a group's attention at home is described with the stage word.
senses.whyCN: 能在家里留住一群人注意力的人，就用舞台上的词来描述。

intro.en: Entertainer is entertain plus the English suffix -er, with the verb coming from Old French entretenir, to hold together.
intro.cn: entertainer 是 entertain 加英语词尾 -er，动词来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Tenir continues the verb for holding.
items.cn: tenir 延续表示「握住」的动词。

items.en: Entretenir means to keep together or maintain.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 提供基础动词。

items.en: The -er noun appears for people who amuse audiences.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，出现指娱乐观众的 -er 名词。

items.en: Entertainer covers stage, screen, and social life.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entertainer 涵盖舞台、屏幕与社交生活。

note.en: Entertainer is the person noun of entertain, and it sits near performer and host words.
note.cn: entertainer 是 entertain 的人物名词，与 performer 和 host 类词相邻。

entries.definition: to amuse or receive guests
shows or activities that amuse
amusing and enjoyable
a person who acts, sings, or dances for an audience
a person who creates or performs art
a person who receives guests or presents a show

normalIntro.en: Entertainer is simply entertain plus -er, so it names the person who holds an audience.
normalIntro.cn: entertainer 就是 entertain 加 -er，指那个留住观众的人。

normal.en: Add -er to entertain and you get the person who does it.
normal.cn: 在 entertain 后加 -er，就得到做这件事的人。

normal.en: The -er ending appears in teacher and singer in exactly the same way.
normal.cn: -er 词尾在 teacher 与 singer 中也是同样的用法。

normal.en: An entertainer holds attention, and the audience gives it freely.
normal.cn: 表演者留住注意力，而观众是自愿给出的。

normal.en: Entertainment is the show, while entertainer is the one on stage.
normal.cn: entertainment 是节目，entertainer 是台上的那个人。

normal.en: Compare performer: every entertainer performs, but not every performer entertains.
normal.cn: 对比 performer：每位 entertainer 都在表演，但并非每位 performer 都能娱乐人。

abstract.en: Picture a single spotlight finding one person at the edge of the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光打在舞台边缘的一个人身上。

abstract.en: Imagine a room going quiet, then breaking into applause.
abstract.cn: 想象房间先安静下来，随后爆发出掌声。

abstract.en: Think of a smile passed from the stage to the back row.
abstract.cn: 想象一个微笑从舞台传到最后一排。

examples.en: The entertainer kept the whole room laughing.
examples.cn: 这位表演者让整个房间笑声不断。

examples.en: She works as a children's entertainer at parties.
examples.cn: 她在聚会上做儿童娱乐表演。

examples.en: A good entertainer knows how to read the audience.
examples.cn: 好的表演者懂得如何读懂观众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「entertain + er」——做 entertain 这件事的人，就是表演者；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）→ 中古英语 entretinen → entertain（招待、娱乐）＋ -er → entertainer（表演者）。

sensesIntro.en: The person noun grows straight out of the verb: one who holds attention on stage, one who holds guests at home, and one who holds a party together.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个人物名词直接从动词生长出来：在舞台上留住注意力的人、在家里留住客人的人、把聚会维系起来的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure on a lit stage holding a whole audience's attention.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光下的一个身影，握住全场观众的注意力。

branches.en: The professional performer is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 职业表演者，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: The good host carries the old hospitality sense.
branches.cn: 好客的主人延续古老的待客义项。

branches.en: The lively guest keeps a social gathering amused.
branches.cn: 活泼的人让社交聚会保持欢乐。

branches.en: Stage and home both need someone who holds attention.
branches.cn: 舞台与家庭都需要能留住注意力的人。

branches.en: Professional charm and social charm share the same skill.
branches.cn: 职业魅力与社交魅力共享同一种本领。

intro.en: Entertainer is an English -er noun built on entertain, whose core is a Latin verb for holding.
intro.cn: entertainer 是建立在 entertain 上的英语 -er 名词，其核心是表示「握住」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold; French entretenir means to keep together, and English adds -er for the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 表示握住；法语 entretenir 表示使相聚，英语再加 -er 表示人。

items.example: Entertain is the base of the noun.

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment is the result of entertaining.
items.exampleCN: entertainment 是娱乐行为的结果。

definition_zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事
definition_en: kindness shown to someone who could be punished or harmed, the act of forgiving, or a fortunate relief
core_image: 一只本可以落下的手，停在半空，改成了轻轻扶一把
scene: 法庭上，受害者家属沉默许久，最后没有要求最重的刑罚。 The judge showed mercy and gave the young man a suspended sentence.
sceneCN: 这里是「仁慈、宽恕」（第 1 个义项：对有权惩罚的人手下留情）；句意为法官动了仁慈之心，判这个年轻人缓刑。图中可辨识物件：法庭木栏、卷宗、法官席。

pos.zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事

derivatives.zh: 由 mercy 去 y 加 -ful 构成，义为「仁慈的；慈悲的」
由 mercy 去 y 加 -less 构成，义为「无情的；残忍的」
由 merciful 加 -ly 构成，义为「仁慈地；幸好」

senses.title: Compassion toward someone in your power
senses.definition: kindness and forgiveness shown to someone you have the power to punish or harm
senses.definitionCN: 对你本可以惩罚或伤害的人所表现的善意与宽容
senses.example: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。
senses.why: The Latin word first meant a reward or a price paid; Christian writers used it for the unearned favour God gives, and that idea of a gift nobody earned became human compassion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初指「报酬、代价」；基督教作者用它表示上帝白白赐下的恩惠，而「不配得却得到的礼物」这一想法，后来变成了人对人的怜悯。

senses.title: Forgiveness instead of punishment
senses.definition: the act of forgiving an offender or treating them less severely than the rules allow
senses.definitionCN: 原谅犯错者，或对其处理得比规定更宽大
senses.example: She begged the court for mercy.
senses.exampleCN: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。
senses.why: Once mercy is a favour granted rather than earned, it naturally appears in courts, where the powerful can choose to relax the full weight of the law.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mercy 是不配得而得到的恩惠，它自然出现在法庭上——掌权者可以选择减轻法律的全力压迫。

senses.title: A fortunate relief
senses.definition: a welcome event that brings relief from pain or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 带来解脱、令人庆幸的事，使人脱离痛苦或困境
senses.example: It was a mercy that the fever broke before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 烧在黎明前退了，真是件幸事。
senses.why: If mercy is kindness that spares someone, an event that spares us suffering can be called a mercy too, as if the world had chosen to be kind.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mercy 是「手下留情」的善意，那么一件让我们免受痛苦的事也能叫 mercy，就好像这个世界选择对我们仁慈了一回。

senses.title: Completely in someone's power
senses.definition: used in the phrase at the mercy of, meaning completely controlled by another person or force
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 at the mercy of，意为完全受某人或某种力量支配
senses.example: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 小船只能任凭风摆布。
senses.why: To be at someone's mercy is to stand where their kindness or cruelty decides your fate, so the phrase pictures a person wholly handed over to another's will.
senses.whyCN: at someone's mercy 就是站在「对方的仁慈或残忍决定你命运」的位置上，这个短语画出一个人被完全交到别人意志里的样子。

intro.en: Mercy goes back to a Latin word for wages and price, and its move from payment to pardon is one of the most striking shifts in English.
intro.cn: mercy 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「报酬、代价」的词，它从「付钱」转向「宽恕」，是英语里最引人注目的词义变化之一。

items.en: Merces meant pay, wages or a price, the reward owed for work or for a service.
items.cn: merces 意为报酬、工资或代价，即为工作或服务应付的回报。

items.en: Christian writers used merces for the free favour and pardon given by God, a gift not earned by the receiver.
items.cn: 基督教作者用 merces 表示上帝白白赐予的恩惠与赦免，是接受者并未挣得的礼物。

items.en: Old French merci carried the sense of pity and mercy, and also served as a word of thanks.
items.cn: 古法语 merci 带有怜悯与仁慈的意思，同时也用作道谢之词。

items.en: Middle English mercy named both the virtue of compassion and the act of sparing an offender.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mercy 既指仁慈这种德性，也指饶恕犯错者的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the courtly and religious senses and adds the everyday phrase at the mercy of.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法庭与宗教两方面的含义，又增添了日常短语 at the mercy of。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin root for trade and reward; the near-meaning group gathers words for compassion and forgiveness.
note.cn: 形近组收来自拉丁语「交易、报酬」词根的词；近义组收表示怜悯与宽恕的词。

entries.definition: A soldier who fights for pay; from Latin mercenarius, from merces, wages.
entries.definitionCN: 为报酬而战的士兵；来自拉丁语 mercenarius，源出 merces（报酬）。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells goods; from Latin mercari, to trade, from merx, merchandise.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖货物的人；来自拉丁语 mercari（做买卖），源出 merx（货物）。

entries.definition: Goods for sale; built on the Latin root merc-, trade.
entries.definitionCN: 待售的商品；建立在表示「交易」的拉丁词根 merc- 上。

entries.definition: Relating to trade and commerce; from the same Latin trading root.
entries.definitionCN: 与贸易、商业有关的；来自同一拉丁「交易」词根。

entries.definition: Sympathy for the suffering of others, with a wish to help.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情，并希望帮上一把。

entries.definition: A feeling of sorrow for someone's misfortune.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人不幸的难过之情。

entries.definition: The act of pardoning someone who has done wrong.
The quality of punishing less severely than allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 处罚比规定更宽大的做法。

normalIntro.en: The word moved from a price paid to a pardon given, and its family keeps the twin ideas of earning and giving.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「付出的代价」走向「给予的宽恕」，它的同族词则一直保留「挣得」与「给予」两条线索。

normal.en: Merces in Latin is wages or a price, so mercy begins in the world of payment and debt.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merces 是工资或代价，所以 mercy 最初属于「付钱与欠债」的世界。

normal.en: Christian Latin turned the word into God's free pardon, a gift the receiver could never earn.
normal.cn: 基督教拉丁语把这个词转为上帝白白的赦免，是接受者永远挣不到的礼物。

normal.en: Merchant and merchandise keep the trading sense of the same root, which is why they look and sound like mercy.
normal.cn: merchant 与 merchandise 保留同一词根的交易义，所以它们看起来、听起来都像 mercy。

normal.en: Merciful adds -ful to mercy, meaning full of mercy; merciless adds -less, meaning without it.
normal.cn: merciful 在 mercy 后加 -ful，意为「充满仁慈」；merciless 加 -less，意为「没有仁慈」。

normal.en: At the mercy of is a fixed phrase: the person stands exactly where another's kindness decides what happens.
normal.cn: at the mercy of 是固定短语：这个人就站在「别人的仁慈决定结果」的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that stops halfway down and turns into a hand that lifts someone up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只已经抬起、准备落下的手，在半空停住，变成一只把人扶起的手。

abstract.en: Mercy is power that chooses not to spend itself.
abstract.cn: mercy 是选择不把力量全部用出去的力量。

abstract.en: A price and a pardon in one word reminds us that forgiving always costs someone something.
abstract.cn: 「代价」与「赦免」同处一词，提醒人：宽恕总要有人付出点什么。

examples.en: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
examples.cn: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。

examples.en: She begged the court for mercy.
examples.cn: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。

examples.en: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
examples.cn: 小船只能任凭风摆布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事」——本来要重罚，结果说没事；mercy 就是宽恕。

root: 拉丁语 merces（报酬、代价）经基督教拉丁语转为「上帝的恩惠」，再经古法语 merci（怜悯）进入英语；同族词多与交易、报酬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is kindness that spares; it branches into courtroom forgiveness, fortunate relief, and the phrase for being wholly in another's power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手下留情的善意」；由此分出法庭上的宽恕、令人庆幸的解脱，以及表示完全受制于人的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that could strike, held back and turned into a hand that lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只本可以打下去的手，收住了，变成一只扶人的手。

branches.en: a judgement seat where the heavier sentence is set aside
branches.cn: 审判席上，较重的刑罚被放到一边

branches.en: a court where the rules are deliberately softened
branches.cn: 法庭上有意把规矩放松一些

branches.en: a fever breaking before dawn
branches.cn: 烧在黎明前退了下去

branches.en: a small boat drifting where the wind sends it
branches.cn: 小船随风漂到哪里就是哪里

branches.en: the same spared outcome, given as feeling and as act
branches.cn: 同一种「免于受罚」的结果，一面是心软，一面是行为

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for pay and price, a Latin trading root, and two English suffixes for having and lacking a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示报酬与代价的拉丁名词、一个拉丁交易词根，以及两个表示「有」与「无」某种性质的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin noun of pay and a trading root stand behind the French word that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 一个表示报酬的拉丁名词与一个交易词根，支撑着英语借来的法语词形。

definition_en: the legal status of belonging to a country; also an ethnic group sharing origin, language or culture, and the people of a nation as a whole
core_image: 一本深色护照翻开，第一页印着国徽和持照人的脸
scene: 机场入境大厅的队伍缓缓前移，人人手里攥着一本深色护照。 Her nationality was printed on the first page of the passport.
sceneCN: 这里 nationality 是「国籍」（第 1 个义项：法律上的归属）；句意为她的国籍印在护照第一页。图中可辨识物件：护照、国徽、入境通道。

derivatives.zh: 由 nation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「国家的；民族的」
与 nationality 同出拉丁语 natio（出生、族群），义为「国家；民族」
由 national 加 -ism 构成，义为「民族主义」
由 national 加 -ist 构成，义为「民族主义者」

senses.title: Legal membership of a country
senses.definition: the legal status of belonging to a particular country, which brings rights and duties
senses.definitionCN: 法律上归属于某个国家的身份，伴随相应的权利和义务
senses.example: She holds dual nationality.
senses.exampleCN: 她拥有双重国籍。
senses.why: The Latin stem natio first named a group born in the same place, and the legal sense grows when a state turns that shared birth into formal membership.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 natio 最初指在同一地方出生的一群人，当国家把共同的出生变成正式身份时，法律义「国籍」就长出来了。

senses.title: An ethnic group with a shared origin
senses.definition: a group of people who share ancestry, language or culture, whether or not they have their own state
senses.definitionCN: 共享血统、语言或文化的人群，无论是否建立自己的国家
senses.example: The region is home to more than twenty nationalities.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区居住着二十多个民族。
senses.why: Since natio meant a people born together, it naturally names ethnic groups before it names passports.
senses.whyCN: 既然 natio 指一同出生的一群人，它先用来指民族群体，然后才用来指护照上的身份。

senses.title: The people of a nation taken as a whole
senses.definition: the whole body of people belonging to a nation, considered together
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个国家的全体人民，作为整体来看
senses.example: The whole nationality stood behind the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 全体国民都支持这项改革。
senses.why: A nationality can be counted one by one, but it can also be spoken of as a single body, which is why the word can mean the people collectively.
senses.whyCN: nationality 可以一个一个地数，也可以当作一个整体来说，所以它能指全体国民。

intro.en: Nationality reaches back through French to the Latin verb nasci, to be born, because a people was first understood as those born together.
intro.cn: nationality 经法语上溯到拉丁动词 nasci（出生），因为一群人最初就被理解为「一同出生的人」。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, and it supplied the whole family of words about birth and origin.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，派生出整族与出生、来源有关的词。

items.en: Natio named a group of people born in the same place, a tribe or a people, rather than a state.
items.cn: natio 指在同一地方出生的一群人，即部落或民族，而不是国家。

items.en: Old French took natio as nacion, still naming a people or a stock.
items.cn: 古法语把 natio 写作 nacion，仍指民族或血统。

items.en: English nationality appears in the seventeenth century and begins to cover legal membership of a state.
items.cn: 英语里 nationality 于十七世纪出现，开始包含对国家法律身份的归属。

items.en: Modern usage separates the passport sense from the ethnic sense, and both remain common.
items.cn: 现代用法把护照上的国籍义与民族义分开，而两者都很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same birth stem; the near-meaning group collects words about citizenship and ethnic identity.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出生」词干上的词；近义组收关于公民身份与族群认同的词。

entries.definition: A large community of people with a shared history and state.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有共同历史与国家的庞大群体；民族；国家。

entries.definition: Belonging to a whole country rather than to a region.
entries.definitionCN: 属于整个国家的，而非某个地区的。

entries.definition: Present from birth, not learned.
The legal position of being a citizen of a country.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某国公民的法律身份；公民身份。

entries.definition: The fact of belonging to a particular ethnic group.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某个族群的事实；族群属性。

entries.definition: The whole body of citizens of a country.

normalIntro.en: The word moves from a people born together to a legal status, and its endings mark each step of that journey.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「一同出生的一群人」走到一种法律身份，几个词尾标记了这段路程。

normal.en: Nation and nationality share the Latin stem nat-, born, so the word is about where a person comes from.
normal.cn: nation 与 nationality 共用拉丁词干 nat-（出生），所以这个词说的是人从哪里来。

normal.en: National adds -al to nation; nationality adds -ity to national, turning a description into a status.
normal.cn: national 在 nation 后加 -al；nationality 在 national 后加 -ity，把描述变成一种身份。

normal.en: Dual nationality is a fixed phrase, and the adjective dual never changes with the noun.
normal.cn: dual nationality 是固定搭配，dual 这个形容词不随名词变化。

normal.en: Minority nationality is the usual phrase in Chinese English for an ethnic group smaller than the majority.
normal.cn: minority nationality 是中国英语里指少数族群常用的说法。

normal.en: Citizenship is the everyday word for rights, nationality the legal and formal word for status.
normal.cn: citizenship 是讲权利的日常说法，nationality 是讲身份的法律正式说法。

abstract.en: A word built on birth reminds us that a passport is a piece of paper laid over the fact of where someone was born.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「出生」之上的词提醒人：护照只是盖在「人在何处出生」这个事实之上的一张纸。

abstract.en: Nationality can be one person's paper and a whole people's name at the same time, which is why it feels both personal and political.
abstract.cn: nationality 既可以是某人的一张纸，也可以是一整群人的名字，所以它既私人又政治。

abstract.en: When the same word covers a passport and a people, identity is being asked to carry two very different weights.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指护照又指民族，说明身份这个概念被迫承担两种很不同的重量。

examples.en: She has dual nationality.
examples.cn: 她拥有双重国籍。

examples.en: People of many nationalities live in the capital.
examples.cn: 首都居住着许多不同民族的人。

examples.en: The law grants nationality to children born here.
examples.cn: 法律赋予在此出生的孩子国籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿新人来提」——递上材料换本新护照，记住 nationality 是国籍。

root: 拉丁语 nasci（出生）→ natio（一同出生的人群、民族）→ 古法语 nacion → 英语 nationality（十七世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a group born together; from it the word divides into legal nationality, ethnic group and the people as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一同出生的一群人；由此分出法律上的国籍、民族群体以及作为整体的国民。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark passport opening to show a crest and a face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色护照翻开，露出国徽与持照人的脸。

branches.en: a stamp coming down on the first page of a new passport
branches.cn: 一枚印章落在新护照的第一页

branches.en: a queue of travellers holding books of different colours
branches.cn: 旅客排成长队，手里拿着不同颜色的护照

branches.en: a village where several languages are spoken at one market
branches.cn: 一个集市上同时有人讲几种语言的村庄

branches.en: a festival with costumes from many ethnic groups
branches.cn: 汇聚许多族群服饰的节日

branches.en: a whole crowd singing one anthem in a square
branches.cn: 广场上整片人群齐唱一首国歌

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin stem for birth, a noun ending and a further ending that turns a description into a status.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「出生」的拉丁词干、名词词尾，以及把描述变成身份的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 空的；空缺的；空闲的；茫然的
definition_en: empty and not occupied, free for someone to take, or showing no thought
core_image: 一间搬空的屋子，只剩地上一块没被晒褪色的方印
scene: 楼下的门上贴着招租的纸条，窗帘全拆了，从街上能看见里面空荡的墙。 The flat has been vacant since the family left in spring.
sceneCN: 这里 vacant 是「空的、无人居住的」（第 1 个义项：无人占用）；句意为这家人春天搬走后，这套房子一直空着。搬空屋子里的方印，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加抽象名词后缀 -cy，义为「空缺；空房」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「茫然地」
同根动词，义为「腾出；空出」
同根名词，义为「假期」

senses.title: Empty and not occupied
senses.definition: of a room, seat, or building, empty because nobody is using it
senses.definitionCN: 形容房间、座位或建筑无人使用而空着
senses.example: The seat beside her stayed vacant for the whole journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途中她旁边的座位一直空着。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to be empty or free, and the adjective simply names that state of being left unoccupied.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「空着、闲置」，形容词只是把这种无人占用的状态命名出来。

senses.title: A job or position with nobody in it
senses.definition: of a job or post that no one holds at present
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个职位目前无人担任
senses.example: The manager's post fell vacant in June.
senses.exampleCN: 经理一职在六月空了出来。
senses.why: A post is like a seat in an office: when the holder leaves, the place stays empty and waits to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 职位就像办公室里的一把椅子：任职者走了，位置就空在那里等有人补上。

senses.title: Free from duties, unoccupied time
senses.definition: of time or a person, free from work or duty
senses.definitionCN: 形容时间或人没有工作与职责在身
senses.example: In his vacant hours he walks along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 空闲的时候他就沿着运河散步。
senses.why: If the space is empty, the person is free; the word transfers easily from places to hours and to people.
senses.whyCN: 空间空着，人也就被腾出来了；这个词很容易从地方转到时间与人身上。

senses.title: Showing no thought or interest
senses.definition: of a look or expression that shows no thought or attention
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼神或表情里没有想法与注意
senses.example: He gave a vacant stare when asked about the date.
senses.exampleCN: 问他日子时，他茫然地瞪着眼。
senses.why: An empty room has nothing in it, and a face with nothing behind it looks the same way, so the word crosses over.
senses.whyCN: 空屋子里面什么都没有，面上背后什么都没有的样子也一样，于是词义就这么挪了过去。

senses.title: Of no force, empty of effect
senses.definition: in legal and formal use, having no force or holder
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与正式用语中，指没有效力或没有持有者
senses.example: The promise was vacant because nothing was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 因为什么都没签，那句承诺并无实效。
senses.why: Law borrows the plain idea of emptiness to say that a right or a promise has nothing inside it.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了最朴素的「空」来说明某项权利或诺言里面没有实质内容。

intro.en: From Latin vacare, to be empty, through French; the same root gives vacation and vacuum.
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 vacare（空着），经法语进入英语；同一词根也给出 vacation 与 vacuum。

items.en: Vacare meant to be empty, free, or at leisure, and vacans was its present participle.
items.cn: vacare 意为「空着、自由、有闲」，vacans 是它的现在分词。

items.en: Vacant entered French as a legal word for property and offices with no holder.
items.cn: vacant 作为法律用词进入法语，指无人占有的产业与职位。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century, first for empty land and posts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，最初用于空地与空缺职位。

items.en: The phrase vacant possession fixes the sense of an empty house handed over.
items.cn: vacant possession 这一说法固定了「交房时已腾空」的含义。

items.en: From empty rooms the word passes to blank expressions and to rights with no force.
items.cn: 从空房间出发，词义又转到茫然的神情与没有效力的权利上。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the vac- family, and the near-meaning group contrasts empty with occupied and busy.
note.cn: 形近组收集 vac- 词族，近义组把空着与占用、忙碌对照起来。

to leave a place empty
a period free from work
a space with no matter in it
having nothing inside

normalIntro.en: One Latin idea of being empty runs through the vac- family: vacant, vacancy, vacate, vacation, vacuum.
normalIntro.cn: 「空着」这一个拉丁概念贯穿 vac- 词族：vacant、vacancy、vacate、vacation、vacuum。

normal.en: A vacant post and a vacant seat both mean a place waiting for someone.
normal.cn: vacant post 与 vacant seat 都指等着人来的位置。

normal.en: A vacant look is the figurative use and very common in novels.
normal.cn: vacant look 是引申用法，在小说里十分常见。

normal.en: Vacancy is the noun for both an empty room and an unfilled job.
normal.cn: vacancy 既是空房，也是空缺职位。

normal.en: The verb vacate is the action behind the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词背后的动作就是动词 vacate。

normal.en: Hotels say no vacancy when every room is taken.
normal.cn: 旅馆满房时会说 no vacancy。

abstract.en: Picture a bare room with a pale square where a picture hung.
abstract.cn: 想象空屋子里墙上留下一块没褪色的方印。

abstract.en: Hear a landlord tape a renting notice to a door.
abstract.cn: 听房东往门上贴招租纸条。

abstract.en: See someone answer a question with eyes that focus on nothing.
abstract.cn: 看有人回答问题时眼神落在空处。

examples.en: There are two vacant rooms on the second floor.
examples.cn: 二楼有两个空房间。

examples.en: The teaching post has been vacant since last summer.
examples.cn: 这个教职从去年夏天起一直空着。

examples.en: He stared at the map with a vacant expression.
examples.cn: 他茫然地盯着地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「未垦」——还没被开垦的地荒着，也就是空着没人用。

root: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、有闲）的现在分词 vacans，经古法语 vacant 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: Empty space, then an unfilled post, then free time, then a face with nothing behind it, and finally a right with no force.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是空出的地方，再是没人担任的职位，再是空出的时间，再是背后空无一物的表情，最后是没有效力的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare room with a pale square on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：空屋子里墙上那块浅色方印。

branches.en: The space branch: a place with nobody using it.
branches.cn: 空间分支：没人使用的地方。

branches.en: The job branch: a working place waiting to be filled.
branches.cn: 职位分支：等待补人的工作岗位。

branches.en: The time branch: hours with no duty attached.
branches.cn: 时间分支：没有职责的小时。

branches.en: The face branch: eyes with nothing focused on them.
branches.cn: 表情分支：目光没有落点。

branches.en: The formal branch: emptiness in law and in offices.
branches.cn: 正式分支：法律与职位上的「空」。

intro.en: A Latin root of emptiness with an adjective ending: literally being empty.
intro.cn: 一个表示「空」的拉丁词根加形容词词尾：字面就是「空着的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacare, to be empty or at leisure, gives vacans and the noun vacatio; the endings -ant and -ance are its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、有闲）给出 vacans 与名词 vacatio；英语形式为词尾 -ant 与 -ance。

items.exampleCN: 词根 vac- 承载「空」义。
vacant 意为处于空着的状态。

items.example: Vacancy names the empty state or room.
items.exampleCN: vacancy 命名空着的状态或房间。

items.example: Vacate means to make a place empty.
Vacation once meant the act of vacating.
items.exampleCN: vacation 早先指腾空这一行为。

items.example: Vacuum is a Latin-style noun of emptiness.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 是拉丁式的「空」名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to be empty, to be free

definition_en: to turn around a center, to take turns, or to change crops in a field
core_image: 绕轴转动的车轮
scene: 地球绕着自己的轴旋转。 The earth rotates on its axis.
sceneCN: 这里 rotate 是「旋转」（第 1 个义项）；句意：地球绕着自己的轴旋转。

derivatives.zh: 旋转；轮换
旋转器
旋转的
旋转的；轮转的

senses.title: Turn around
senses.definition: to turn around a fixed point or center
senses.definitionCN: 绕一个固定点或中心转动
senses.example: The wheel rotates very smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个轮子转得很顺。
senses.why: The object turns around its own center.
senses.whyCN: 物体绕自身中心转动。

senses.title: Take turns
senses.definition: to change places or duties in a regular order
senses.definitionCN: 按固定顺序更换位置或职责
senses.example: The staff rotate between day and night shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 员工在白天与夜班之间轮换。
senses.why: People take turns in a circle of duties.
senses.whyCN: 人们在一圈职责中轮流承担。

senses.title: Rotate crops
senses.definition: to change the type of crop grown in a field each season
senses.definitionCN: 每季更换田地中种植的作物种类
senses.example: Farmers rotate wheat with beans.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把小麦与豆类轮作。
senses.why: Fields take turns growing different plants.
senses.whyCN: 田地轮流种植不同作物。

intro.en: Rotate comes from Latin rota, a wheel.
intro.cn: rotate 源自拉丁语 rota，意为车轮。

items.en: Rota means a wheel.
items.cn: rota 意为车轮。

items.en: Rotare means to turn like a wheel.
items.cn: rotare 意为像车轮一样转动。

items.en: Rotatus is the past participle of turning.
items.cn: rotatus 是表示转动的过去分词。

items.en: English rotate keeps the wheel motion.
items.cn: 英语 rotate 保留车轮转动的意象。

items.en: Rotate extends to shifts and crops.
items.cn: rotate 扩展到轮班与轮作。

note.en: Rotate is turning around a center; revolve is going around another point.
note.cn: rotate 是绕自身中心转，revolve 则绕另一点运行。

entries.definition: turning around a center
the act of turning
a thing that rotates
to move around

normalIntro.en: Rotate is the wheel's motion, shared by people and fields.
normalIntro.cn: rotate 是轮子的运动，也被人和田地借用。

normal.en: The fan rotates above the table.
normal.cn: 风扇在桌子上方旋转。

normal.en: The moon rotates around the earth.
normal.cn: 月球绕地球转动。

normal.en: Nurses rotate between the two wards.
normal.cn: 护士在两个病区之间轮换。

normal.en: Farmers rotate corn with soybeans.
normal.cn: 农民把玉米与大豆轮作。

normal.en: The staff rotate through every department.
normal.cn: 员工轮流到每个部门工作。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel spinning on a still axle.
abstract.cn: 想象车轮在静止的轴上转动。

abstract.en: Imagine people stepping around a circle in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象人们依次绕圈换位。

abstract.en: Think of fields changing their crop each year.
abstract.cn: 想象田地每年更换作物。

examples.en: The earth rotates once every twenty-four hours.
examples.cn: 地球每二十四小时自转一周。

examples.en: The two teams rotate the meeting chair.
examples.cn: 两个团队轮流担任会议主持。

examples.en: We rotate the crops to keep the soil rich.
examples.cn: 我们轮作作物以保持土壤肥沃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel spinning on its axle.

branches.en: Turning around a center is the core sense.

branches.en: People take turns in a circle.

branches.en: Fields take turns with crops.
branches.cn: 田地轮流种植作物。

branches.en: Rotation works as planned change.

intro.cn: rotate 经 rotare 来自拉丁语 rota（车轮）。

latinIntro.en: Rota gives rotare, rotatus, rotation, and rotary.
latinIntro.cn: rota 给出 rotare、rotatus、rotation 与 rotary。

definition_en: a small printed piece of paper that gives a discount or can be exchanged for something
core_image: 一张从报纸上剪下的小纸片，边上留着虚线齿孔
scene: 结账时她从钱包里抽出一张剪下来的小纸片，抵掉了两块零钱。 She handed the cashier a coupon for the soap.
sceneCN: 这里 coupon 指「优惠券」（第 1 个义项：结账时抵扣钱款的小纸片）；句意是她把一张肥皂优惠券递给收银员。

senses.title: A ticket that cuts the price
senses.definition: a printed ticket that takes money off what you buy
senses.definitionCN: 买东西时能减掉一部分钱的印刷票据
senses.example: She saved five dollars with a coupon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一张优惠券省了五块钱。
senses.why: A small promise of a lower price, printed on paper.
senses.whyCN: 把「价格更低」这个承诺印在一张小纸上。

senses.title: A paper exchanged for a gift
senses.definition: a printed piece of paper that can be exchanged for a service or a gift
senses.definitionCN: 可用来换取某项服务或赠品的印刷纸片
senses.example: The coupon entitles you to one free drink.
senses.exampleCN: 这张券让你免费得到一杯饮料。
senses.why: Paper stands in for the thing you will receive.
senses.whyCN: 纸片先替你将要点到的东西站在这里。

senses.title: An interest slip on a bond
senses.definition: a detachable part of a bond that is clipped off to claim interest
senses.definitionCN: 债券上可剪下来领取利息的附券
senses.example: He clipped the coupon and collected the interest.
senses.exampleCN: 他剪下息票，领走了利息。
senses.why: Every payment once had its own small paper to cut.
senses.whyCN: 从前每一笔利息都有一张小纸片等着被剪下。

intro.en: Coupon comes from French couper, to cut, itself from Latin colpus, a stroke or blow.
intro.cn: coupon 源自法语 couper（切），其更早的来源是拉丁语 colpus（击打）。

items.en: Colpus meant a stroke or a blow.
items.cn: colpus 意为一次击打。

items.en: Couper meant to cut something off.
items.cn: couper 意为把某物切下来。

items.en: Coupon named a piece cut from a larger sheet.
items.cn: coupon 指从大张纸上切下的一小片。

items.en: English coupon first named an interest slip cut from a bond.
items.cn: 英语 coupon 最初指从债券上剪下的息票。

items.en: It now usually means a ticket that cuts the price.
items.cn: 今天它通常指能减价的票据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coup- shape, and the meaning group names other papers of value.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coup- 这一词形，近义组列出其他有价票据的说法。

entries.definition: a sudden and clever success
a car with two doors and a low roof
a throat illness of young children
a paper that can be used as money
a small object or card that stands for value
entries.definitionCN: 代表某种价值的小物件或卡片

entries.definition: a printed card that lets you enter or travel
entries.definitionCN: 允许入场或乘车的印刷卡片

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a slip cut from a sheet, then move to a free drink and to bond interest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从大纸上剪下的小片开始，再到一杯免费饮料，最后到债券利息。

normal.en: Coupon begins with coup, a cut: it is a piece cut from a sheet.
normal.cn: coupon 开头是 coup（切）：它是从大张纸上切下的一片。

normal.en: The dotted line is there so your fingers know where to cut.
normal.cn: 虚线印在那里，是为了让手指知道该从哪儿剪。

normal.en: A coupon is a price cut carried in your pocket.
normal.cn: 优惠券就是装在口袋里的降价。

normal.en: Older bonds paid you by slips you clipped at the edge.
normal.cn: 旧时债券靠你从边上剪下的票券付息。

normal.en: If the paper can be exchanged, it is a coupon.
normal.cn: 只要这张纸能换东西，它就是券。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scissors resting beside a newspaper page.
abstract.cn: 想象一把剪刀搁在报纸页旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a small slip across the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张小票推过柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with a corner torn away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价格标签被撕掉一角。

examples.en: This coupon is valid until the end of June.
examples.cn: 这张优惠券有效期到六月底。

examples.en: He collected coupons from the newspaper every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他每个星期天都从报纸上剪优惠券。

examples.en: You can redeem the coupon at any branch.
examples.cn: 你可以在任何一家分店兑换这张券。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coupon 记成 coup（切）加 on：从大张纸上切下来的一小片，就是能换东西的券。

root: 源自法语 couper（切），再往前是拉丁语 colpus（击打）；coupon 本指从大张纸上剪下的一小片纸，后指可剪下兑取的息票与优惠券。

sensesIntro.en: From a slip cut off a bond, to a paper that lowers a price, to a paper that buys a gift.
sensesIntro.cn: 从债券上剪下的票，到能降价的纸片，最后到能换赠品的纸片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small slip cut from a larger printed sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：从大张印刷纸上剪下的一小片。

branches.en: The slip carries a promise of paying less.
branches.cn: 这张小片带着少付一点钱的承诺。

branches.en: The same slip can stand for a drink or a gift.
branches.cn: 同样的小片也能代表一杯饮料或一份赠品。

branches.en: On old bonds the slip was cut to claim interest.
branches.cn: 在旧债券上，剪下这张小片就能领息。

branches.en: Both are paper that buys something without money.
branches.cn: 两者都是不用钱就买到东西的纸。

branches.en: A coupon is always a claim waiting to be clipped.
branches.cn: 优惠券永远是一张等着被剪下的索取凭据。

intro.en: Coupon is built on the French cutting base coup-, extended by the noun ending -on.
intro.cn: coupon 建立在法语表示切的词基 coup- 上，再加名词词尾 -on。

latinIntro.en: The cutting base goes back to Latin colpus, a blow, which also shapes coup and recoup.
latinIntro.cn: 表示切的词基可追到拉丁语 colpus（一击），coup 与 recoup 也由它构成。

items.meaning: a slip cut from a sheet

items.example: She keeps coupons in a box.
items.exampleCN: 她把优惠券收在盒子里。

items.example: A keen couponer never pays full price.
items.exampleCN: 爱用券的人从不付全价。

items.example: The coupon book has ten pages.

items.meaning: a set of letters typed for a discount
items.meaningCN: 网上结账时输入的折扣代码
items.example: Enter the coupon code at checkout.
The deal was a coup for the team.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易对团队来说是一次漂亮的胜利。

items.example: They recouped their costs in a year.
items.exampleCN: 他们一年内收回了成本。
